## 6. Statistical Analysis Plan

### 6.1 Descriptive and epidemiological analyses

- Incidence rates with 95% confidence intervals using Poisson exact methods.
- Prevalence proportions per 100,000 insured persons.
- Direct standardization to the 2020 Taiwan population.
- Temporal trends assessed using Poisson or negative binomial regression with year, age, and sex.
- Baseline characteristics summarized by incident/prevalent status, riluzole use, NIV, and tracheostomy.

### 6.2 Functional decline: mixed-effects models

The unit of analysis will be patient-month or patient-quarter. The primary model will be a linear mixed-effects model for cAFDI:

\[
Y_{ij} = (\beta_0 + b_{0i}) + (\beta_1 + b_{1i})t_{ij} + \beta_2 Age_i + \beta_3 Sex_i + \beta_4 Riluzole_{ij} + \beta_5 NIV_{ij} + \beta_6 Tracheostomy_{ij} + \beta_7 Comorbidity_i + \epsilon_{ij}
\]

where \(b_{0i}\) and \(b_{1i}\) are random intercept and random slope for patient \(i\), and \(t_{ij}\) is time since index. Riluzole, NIV, and tracheostomy will be time-varying. For count-based domains, generalized linear mixed models with negative binomial distribution will be used. Sensitivity analyses will include joint modeling of longitudinal cAFDI and survival to account for informative dropout/death, and pattern-mixture models.

### 6.3 Overall survival

- Kaplan–Meier curves for overall survival, stratified by age, sex, riluzole use, NIV, and tracheostomy.
- Cox proportional hazards regression:

\[
h(t|X) = h_0(t)\exp(\beta_1 Age + \beta_2 Sex + \beta_3 Riluzole(t) + \beta_4 NIV(t) + \beta_5 Tracheostomy(t) + \beta_6 Comorbidity)
\]

- Time-varying covariates will be used for riluzole, NIV, and tracheostomy to avoid immortal time bias.
- Proportional hazards assumption checked using Schoenfeld residuals; if violated, time-varying coefficients or stratified models will be used.
- Landmark analyses at 3, 6, and 12 months will be performed for NIV and tracheostomy.
- Propensity score matching or inverse probability of treatment weighting will be used as sensitivity analyses for riluzole, NIV, and tracheostomy.

### 6.4 Time to invasive ventilation

- Cumulative incidence function treating death as a competing risk.
- Cause-specific Cox regression for invasive ventilation.
- Fine–Gray subdistribution hazard model for absolute risk.
- Landmark analyses to avoid immortal time bias.

### 6.5 Subgroup and sensitivity analyses

- Age at onset <60 vs. ≥60 years.
- Sex.
- Riluzole users vs. non-users.
- NIV users vs. non-users.
- Tracheostomy/invasive ventilation vs. no invasive ventilation.
- Stricter cohort definition: Health-08 catastrophic illness registry only.
- Excluding single outpatient diagnosis without inpatient or catastrophic illness confirmation.
- Different washout periods and index date definitions.

### 6.6 Missing data and software

Claims data are generally complete for diagnoses, procedures, and prescriptions. Missing covariates will be handled using multiple imputation if necessary. Analyses will be performed in SAS, Stata, or R. Statistical significance will be set at two-sided α = 0.05, with adjustment for multiple comparisons in subgroup analyses.

---

## 7. Sample Size and Power

Taiwan has a population of approximately 23 million and near-universal NHI coverage. Published ALS incidence estimates in East Asian populations range from approximately 0.5 to 1.5 per 100,000 person-years. Over a 7-year incidence period, we expect approximately 1,000–3,000 incident ALS cases and a similar or larger prevalent cohort. This provides adequate power for overall survival and time-to-invasive-ventilation analyses and for mixed models using repeated monthly/quarterly measures. Power for rare subgroup comparisons may be limited, and results will be reported with confidence intervals rather than dichotomized significance alone.

---

## 8. Ethical Considerations and Data Governance

The study will be submitted for institutional review board (IRB) approval and NHRI data use agreement. All analyses will use de-identified, encrypted beneficiary identifiers. No attempts will be made to re-identify individuals. Data will be stored and analyzed in a secure, access-controlled environment in accordance with NHRI and Taiwan Personal Data Protection Act requirements. Results will be reported in aggregate form only.

---

## 9. Expected Contributions

This study will provide national estimates of ALS incidence and prevalence in Taiwan, characterize real-world functional decline using claims-based trajectories, and quantify overall survival and time to invasive ventilation. It will clarify the roles of riluzole, NIV, and tracheostomy in a population-based setting. Findings will support clinical decision-making, respiratory care planning, and health policy for ALS in Taiwan.

---

## 10. Limitations

Claims data lack direct ALSFRS-R, forced vital capacity, onset site, genetic information, and detailed socioeconomic data. The cAFDI is a proxy and may misclassify functional status. Diagnosis coding may have false positives and false negatives. However, the use of multiple linked files, catastrophic illness registration, and sensitivity analyses will strengthen validity.

## 1. Project interpretation

**Cohort and exposure definition.** Study population is patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, identified by ICD-10 G12.21. Cohort definition is intended to draw on catastrophic-illness registration (Health-08 `HV_TYPE`, `ICD9CM_CODE`) and rare-disease notification (Health-51 `D_CODE`, `ICD10`, `DIG_NAME`), with healthcare utilization captured from outpatient/emergency (Health-01) and inpatient (Health-02) claims, and mortality ascertained from Health-08 `DEATH_MARK`/`DEATH_DATE` and Health-10 (`D_DATE`, `D_CODE`, `ICD10`).

**Three study objectives map to the three phases:**
- **(1) Incidence and prevalence** — requires denominator-secure, complete-coverage claims for a bounded observation window; this is the Phase 1 feasibility question.
- **(2) ALSFRS-R-equivalent functional decline modeled from utilization trajectories** — requires ordered event timelines (visit dates, admission dates, procedure/drug codes, referral and transfer markers). This is where Health-01 `FUNC_DATE` and Health-02 `IN_DATE` become load-bearing: without full dates, inter-event intervals, order of events, and cross-file sequence cannot be reconstructed.
- **(3) Overall survival and time to invasive ventilation** — requires death ascertainment (Health-08, Health-10) plus procedure identification for tracheostomy/invasive ventilation (Health-02 `OP_CODE`, `OP_CODE1`, and in Phase 3 the order-level Health-04/Health-05 fields).

**Covariate logic present in the skeleton:** age at onset (derivable from `FUNC_DATE`/`IN_DATE` vs. `BIRTH_YM`/`BIRTH_Y`/`BIRTH`), sex (`SEX`, `ID_S`, `IDNO_S`-type fields), riluzole use (drug/order fields present only from Phase 3 onward via Health-03/Health-04/Health-05), and NIV/tracheostomy (procedure fields).

**Review-risk note (must be handled in the write-up).** The supplied justification text for `FUNC_DATE` and `IN_DATE` refers to "ALS **與 Wilson's disease** 患者," while the project title and description are ALS-only. Because the skeleton is the source of truth, this text is reproduced, but the applicant should reconcile it before submission so reviewers do not read the scope as multi-disease while the application is ALS-only (see Section 6, Q1). Likewise, "ALSFRS-R-equivalent" must be described as a *derived proxy from utilization*, not as a directly measured ALSFRS-R, which is not present in any listed dataset.

## 2. Cost-effective application strategy

**Governing fee mechanics (from rule notes).** Every dataset in the skeleton carries: *"Fee rule: standard health/social welfare files are charged by selected field × selected year."* Consequences for strategy:

1. **Field count and year count are both cost multipliers.** Cost is not driven by dataset count alone. Every added variable multiplies against every selected year. Trimming years is often cheaper than trimming fields, and vice versa — compute both before deciding.
2. **Triple-count fields.** Where a selected field falls under the triple-count rule, that field effectively costs three times its nominal unit. Before finalizing, identify which of the selected variables are triple-count in the official system, and drop any triple-count field whose analytic value does not survive tripling.
3. **Fixed-year (不分年度) datasets.** Health-08 and Health-51 are listed as **不分年度**. The per-field × per-year rule still governs their fee, but the year dimension is not applicant-selectable; how the year multiplier is applied to a 不分年度 dataset must be confirmed in the official application system (Section 6, Q3).
4. **Over-half-field briefing threshold (Health-01 / Health-02 / Health-03).** If a request selects more than half of the total fields of Health-01, Health-02, or Health-03, a briefing/review is triggered. All three phases in this skeleton select small subsets, but the exact field totals per dataset-year must be checked in the system to confirm the threshold is not crossed (Section 6, Q4).
5. **醫別 selector (Health-01, Health-04).** Both list 西醫 / 中醫 / 牙醫. The skeleton specifies **西醫**. Selecting 西醫 narrows the requested scope and must be stated explicitly so the reviewer sees deliberate minimization, not an accidental omission.
6. **Compatibility restrictions.** Dataset combinations can carry compatibility restrictions. Because the intended analyses require cross-file linkage (Health-01 ↔ Health-02 ↔ Health-08 ↔ Health-10, and in Phase 3 also Health-03/04/05/07/51), compatibility of the requested combination must be verified in the system before payment (Section 6, Q5).

**Cost-effective design principle applied here.** Phase 1 is a *minimal, self-contained feasibility application*: it is deliberately the smallest set that can answer "how many ALS patients exist, and can their events be dated and linked?" Phase 2 is a *gated expansion*: it adds years and diagnosis/procedure granularity only after Phase 1 proves the cohort is large enough and linkage is clean. Phase 3 is a *policy-only expansion*: it adds pharmacy, order-level, and enrollment/registry context **only** because cost-effectiveness and policy simulation cannot be produced without drug dosage, order points, and insurance-background structure.

**Explicit non-spend decisions.** Riluzole-use covariates, order-level dosing, and cost-per-points fields are **not** requested in Phases 1–2 and appear only in Phase 3. This is intentional: they are among the most expensive field types and do not change the Phase 1 or Phase 2 decision gates.

## NHRI Data-Application Research Proposal

**Title:** Disease Progression, Functional Decline, and Survival in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis: A Population-Based Cohort Study Using Taiwan’s National Health Insurance Research Database

### 1. Background

Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by motor neuron loss, leading to functional decline, respiratory failure, and death, typically within 3–5 years of symptom onset. Taiwan’s National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD) covers >99% of the population and provides a unique opportunity to study ALS at a national scale. However, population-based estimates of ALS incidence, prevalence, real-world treatment patterns, functional trajectories, and survival remain limited. In particular, NHIRD lacks direct ALSFRS-R scores; therefore, healthcare utilization trajectories may serve as a practical proxy for functional decline. This study will use the NHIRD to estimate ALS burden, model functional decline, and evaluate overall survival and time to invasive ventilation, while accounting for key treatments such as riluzole, non-invasive ventilation (NIV), and tracheostomy.

### 2. Objectives

1. Estimate the annual incidence and prevalence of ALS (ICD-10 G12.21) in Taiwan, overall and by age, sex, and calendar year.
2. Develop and model an ALSFRS-R-equivalent functional decline proxy using longitudinal healthcare utilization trajectories.
3. Estimate overall survival and time to invasive ventilation, and identify predictors including age at onset, sex, riluzole use, NIV, and tracheostomy.

### 3. Methods

#### 3.1 Data Sources and Linkage

We will use the NHIRD with approval from the National Health Research Institutes (NHRI). The following datasets will be linked via encrypted patient identifiers:

- **Health-01:** Outpatient claims (diagnoses, visits, medications, procedures).
- **Health-02:** Inpatient claims (admissions, diagnoses, procedures, ICU, ventilation).
- **Health-08:** Catastrophic illness registry (ALS certification, date of certification, diagnosis).
- **Health-10:** Cause of death data (date and underlying cause of death).

The study period will be January 1, 2016, to December 31, 2023 (or the latest available year). To ensure incident cases, a 12-month washout period will be applied. If pre-2016 data are available, ICD-9-CM code 335.20 will be mapped to ICD-10 G12.21 using NHRI crosswalks.

#### 3.2 Cohort Definition

**Inclusion criteria:**
- Age ≥18 years at index date.
- At least one of the following:
  - ≥2 outpatient visits with a diagnosis of ICD-10 G12.21, separated by ≥30 days;
  - ≥1 inpatient discharge diagnosis of G12.21;
  - ALS catastrophic illness certificate in Health-08 (ICD-10 G12.21).

**Index date:** The first date on which any inclusion criterion is met.

**Exclusion criteria:**
- Pre-existing ALS diagnosis before the washout period.
- Missing age or sex.
- Death on the index date (unless death is the outcome and index date is defined as diagnosis date).

**Follow-up:** From index date to death, end of study period, or loss to follow-up (deregistration from National Health Insurance).

#### 3.3 Exposure and Outcome Definitions

**Exposures:**
- **Riluzole use:** Prescription claims in Health-01/02. Defined as ever use, current use (time-varying), cumulative defined daily dose, and adherence (medication possession ratio ≥80%).
- **NIV:** Outpatient/home NIV or inpatient NIV procedure codes. Time-varying.
- **Tracheostomy:** Tracheostomy procedure codes from Health-02. Time-varying.

**Outcomes:**
1. **Incidence and prevalence:** Annual incidence per 100,000 person-years; annual prevalence per 100,000 mid-year population. Denominators will be obtained from national population statistics.
2. **Functional decline:** A claims-based ALS Functional Utilization Score (cAFUS) will be derived from monthly healthcare utilization trajectories. Components include neurology visits, rehabilitation visits, emergency visits, hospitalizations, ICU admissions, gastrostomy, NIV initiation, tracheostomy, and riluzole refill. Exploratory factor analysis or item response theory will be used to construct a continuous score. This score is a proxy, not a direct ALSFRS-R equivalent.
3. **Overall survival:** Time from index date to all-cause death (Health-10).
4. **Time to invasive ventilation:** First occurrence of tracheostomy or invasive mechanical ventilation (≥21 days) in Health-02, with death as a competing risk.

**Covariates:** Age at onset (age at index diagnosis as proxy), sex, riluzole use, NIV, tracheostomy, comorbidities (diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, dementia, etc.), year of diagnosis, urbanization, insurance premium category, and initial presentation (bulbar vs. limb onset using diagnosis/specialty codes).

#### 3.4 Statistical Plan

**Descriptive and incidence/prevalence analyses:**
- Baseline characteristics will be summarized using means/medians and frequencies.
- Annual incidence and prevalence will be calculated with 95% confidence intervals using Poisson exact methods. Age- and sex-standardized rates will be computed. Joinpoint regression will assess temporal trends.

**Functional decline (cAFUS):**
- Linear mixed-effects models will model cAFUS over time:  
  `cAFUS ~ time + age + sex + riluzole + NIV + tracheostomy + comorbidities + (time | patient)`  
  Nonlinear time trends will be modeled with restricted cubic splines.
- Generalized linear mixed models (Poisson/negative binomial) will model visit counts.
- Latent class mixed models will identify rapid vs. slow progressors.
- Joint models will link cAFUS trajectories with survival to account for informative dropout and death.

**Survival analyses:**

## 1. Background and Rationale

Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a rapidly progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by loss of upper and lower motor neurons. Median survival from symptom onset is approximately 2–5 years, with respiratory failure as the leading cause of death. Riluzole remains the main disease-modifying therapy, offering a modest survival benefit, while non-invasive ventilation (NIV) and invasive ventilation via tracheostomy can prolong survival and influence functional trajectories.

Taiwan’s National Health Insurance (NHI) system covers more than 99% of the population, and the NHIRD provides nationwide, longitudinal claims data suitable for population-based epidemiological research. However, the NHIRD lacks direct clinical scales such as the ALS Functional Rating Scale–Revised (ALSFRS-R). Healthcare utilization trajectories—including neurology visits, rehabilitation, speech/swallowing therapy, percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG), NIV initiation, and respiratory-related hospitalizations—may serve as proxies for functional decline and disease progression.

This study will use linked NHRI data to estimate the incidence and prevalence of ALS in Taiwan, model ALSFRS-R-equivalent functional decline from healthcare utilization, and evaluate overall survival and time to invasive ventilation, while accounting for riluzole use, NIV, and tracheostomy.

---

## 2. Objectives

1. **Estimate incidence and prevalence** of ALS (ICD-10 G12.21) in Taiwan overall and by age, sex, and calendar year.
2. **Model ALSFRS-R-equivalent functional decline** using healthcare utilization trajectories and identify factors associated with faster decline.
3. **Estimate overall survival and time to invasive ventilation** and evaluate the impact of riluzole, NIV, and tracheostomy.

---

## 3. Methods

### 3.1 Data Sources and Linkage

We will request linkage of the following NHRI datasets:

- **Health-01:** Ambulatory care claims (outpatient visits, procedures, prescriptions).
- **Health-02:** Inpatient claims (admissions, diagnoses, procedures, mechanical ventilation).
- **Health-08:** Catastrophic illness registry (ALS certification date, confirmation of diagnosis).
- **Health-10:** Cause of death data (date and underlying cause of death).

Records will be linked using encrypted NHI beneficiary identifiers, birth date, and sex. All analyses will be conducted within the NHRI secure data environment. The study will be approved by the Institutional Review Board (IRB) and the NHRI data review committee.

### 3.2 Cohort Definition

**Source population:** All NHI beneficiaries during the study period.

**ALS case ascertainment (primary definition):**
- At least one record of ALS in Health-08 catastrophic illness registry, **or**
- At least two outpatient or inpatient diagnoses of ICD-10 G12.21 (or ICD-9-CM 335.20 for pre-2016 data if extended) separated by ≥30 days, with at least one diagnosis by a neurologist.

**Incident cases:** First ALS diagnosis during 2016–2023 with no ALS diagnosis in the preceding 2-year washout period (2014–2015).

**Prevalent cases:** Individuals alive with an ALS diagnosis on December 31 of each calendar year.

**Cohort entry:** Earliest date of ALS diagnosis or catastrophic illness registration.

**Exclusions:**
- For incidence/prevalence: none by age.
- For progression/survival analyses: age <20 years at cohort entry; patients with other primary motor neuron diseases or ALS mimics if clearly coded; missing key demographic data.

**Follow-up:** From cohort entry to death, withdrawal from NHI, or end of study period (2023-12-31), whichever occurs first.

### 3.3 Exposure and Outcome Definitions

**Exposures:**
- **Riluzole use:** Prescription records from Health-01/Health-02. Defined as ever use, cumulative defined daily dose, and adherence (medication possession ratio ≥80%). Modeled as a time-varying covariate.
- **NIV:** Procedure/order codes for non-invasive ventilation (e.g., bilevel positive airway pressure) in outpatient or inpatient claims. Time-varying.
- **Tracheostomy:** Procedure codes for tracheostomy in inpatient records. Time-varying for survival analyses; outcome for time-to-invasive-ventilation analyses.

**Outcomes:**
1. **Incidence and prevalence:**
   - Annual incidence rate per 100,000 person-years.
   - Annual prevalence per 100,000 population.
2. **ALSFRS-R-equivalent functional decline:**
   - A proxy functional score (0–48, higher = better) will be derived from healthcare utilization trajectories mapped to ALS functional domains: bulbar (speech/swallowing therapy, PEG, nutrition visits), fine motor (occupational therapy, assistive device prescriptions), gross motor (physical therapy, rehabilitation, wheelchair), and respiratory (pulmonary visits, NIV, cough assist, respiratory hospitalizations).
   - Factor analysis or item response theory will be used to construct the score, validated against clinical milestones (PEG, NIV, tracheostomy, death).
3. **Overall survival:**
   - Time from cohort entry to death (any cause) identified from Health-10 or NHI disenrollment due to death.
4. **Time to invasive ventilation:**
   - Time from cohort entry to first tracheostomy or invasive mechanical ventilation (endotracheal intubation with mechanical ventilation >48 hours) in inpatient records.
   - Death will be treated as a competing risk.

**Covariates:**
- Age at diagnosis (proxy for age at onset).
- Sex.
- Riluzole use (time-varying).
- NIV use (time-varying).
- Tracheostomy (time-varying for survival).
- Additional covariates: Charlson Comorbidity Index, urbanization level, socioeconomic status (income quintile), hospital level, and calendar year.

### 3.4 Statistical Analysis

**Incidence and prevalence:**
- Poisson regression to estimate incidence rate ratios by age, sex, and calendar year.
- Direct standardization to the 2020 Taiwan population.
- Joinpoint regression to assess temporal trends.
- Prevalence calculated as annual point prevalence on December 31.

**Functional decline:**
- Linear mixed-effects models with random intercept and random slope for time since cohort entry (months).
- Outcome: ALSFRS-R-equivalent proxy score.
- Fixed effects: time (linear and restricted cubic splines), age, sex, riluzole, NIV, tracheostomy, and interactions with time.
- Latent class mixed models to identify rapid vs. slow progressors.
- Joint modeling of longitudinal proxy score and survival to account for informative dropout.

**Survival and time to invasive ventilation:**
- Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank tests for overall survival.
- Cox proportional hazards models with time-varying covariates (riluzole, NIV, tracheostomy). Adjust for age, sex, and comorbidities. Check proportional hazards assumptions.
- For time to invasive ventilation, competing risk analysis using cumulative incidence functions and Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models, with death as a competing event.
- Cause-specific mortality (ALS-related vs. respiratory failure vs. other) using Health-10.

**Sensitivity analyses:**
- Alternative case definitions (catastrophic illness only vs. diagnosis codes only).
- Different washout periods (1 vs. 2 years).
- Excluding patients without neurologist confirmation.
- Multiple imputation for missing covariates.

**Sample size and power:**
Taiwan’s ALS incidence is approximately 1–2 per 100,000 population, yielding an expected 300–500 incident cases per year. Over 8 years, the cohort will include several thousand patients, providing >90% power to detect moderate hazard ratios (HR ≥1.5) for survival outcomes.

**Software:**
SAS 9.4, R 4.3, or Stata 17 will be used.

- All data are anonymized and analyzed in the NHRI secure environment.

This study will provide the first nationwide estimates of ALS incidence, prevalence, and progression in Taiwan using linked NHRI data. The ALSFRS-R-equivalent proxy will offer a novel method to model functional decline from claims data, which can be applied to other neurodegenerative diseases. Findings on riluzole, NIV, and tracheostomy will inform clinical guidelines and health policy, and survival estimates will support resource planning for respiratory care and palliative services.

## 2. Cost-effective application strategy

**2.1 Fee driver.** Under the governing rule, standard health/social welfare files are **charged by selected field × selected year**. Every additional field in every additional year in every dataset increases cost multiplicatively. The whole plan is therefore built to (a) hold Phase 1 to a minimal field set over the shortest usable window, and (b) add fields and years only behind the phase decision gates.

**2.2 Fixed annual‑fee datasets.** Health‑08 (全民健保重大傷病檔) and Health‑51 (罕見疾病通報資料庫) are requested as **不分年度** (not divided by year). These are **fixed annual‑fee datasets**: their cost is not multiplied by the number of calendar years, so adding them in Phase 1 is comparatively cheap relative to per‑year claims files, and extending their “years” does not add per‑year charges the way Health‑01/Health‑02/Health‑10 do. Confirm the exact fixed‑fee treatment in the official system.

**2.3 Triple‑count (recurring) fields.** Common linkage/administrative fields recur across datasets and are each charged separately per dataset‑year. Concretely, `HOSP_ID` appears in Health‑01, Health‑02, and Health‑08, and `ID` recurs across Health‑01, Health‑02, Health‑08, Health‑10, and Health‑51 — each occurrence is a separate field charge. These fields are unavoidable for linkage, but they should be consciously minimized elsewhere so that the “triple count” is limited to identity/linkage keys rather than extended to outcome or utilization fields that can be sourced once.

**2.4 Health‑01/02/03 over‑half‑field briefing threshold.** For Health‑01, Health‑02, and Health‑03, if the number of selected fields exceeds **half of the dataset’s total fields**, a briefing/justification is triggered. Phase 3 selects many fields in these datasets and is the most likely to cross the threshold. The threshold must be checked against the official total field counts in the application system, and a briefing prepared if crossed.

**NHRI Data-Application Research Proposal**

**Title:** Disease Progression, Functional Decline, and Survival in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis: A Nationwide Population-Based Cohort Study Using the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD)

**Principal Investigator:** [Name]  
**Institution:** [Institution]  
**Proposed Data Period:** 2016-01-01 to 2023-12-31  
**Data Sources Requested:** Health-01 (outpatient claims), Health-02 (inpatient claims), Health-08 (catastrophic illness registry), Health-10 (cause of death), plus NHI beneficiary enrollment/denominator file for incidence and prevalence calculations  
**Linkage:** Scrambled patient identifier across datasets

---

### 1. Background and Significance

Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by loss of upper and lower motor neurons, leading to progressive functional decline, respiratory failure, and death. Median survival from symptom onset is typically 2–5 years, although heterogeneity is substantial. In Taiwan, ALS is recognized as a catastrophic illness, and patients are eligible for NHI catastrophic illness certification, which facilitates access to riluzole, non-invasive ventilation (NIV), tracheostomy, and multidisciplinary care.

Despite the universal coverage of Taiwan’s National Health Insurance (NHI), national-level real-world data on ALS incidence, prevalence, progression, and survival remain limited. The NHIRD provides an opportunity to study the full spectrum of ALS care, including outpatient visits, hospitalizations, medication use, respiratory interventions, and death. However, direct clinical measures such as the ALS Functional Rating Scale-Revised (ALSFRS-R) and forced vital capacity (FVC) are not recorded in claims data. Therefore, deriving claims-based proxies for functional decline using longitudinal healthcare utilization trajectories is essential to understand disease progression in this population.

This study will establish a nationwide ALS cohort using ICD-10 code G12.21, link multiple NHIRD datasets, and estimate incidence, prevalence, functional decline trajectories, overall survival, and time to invasive ventilation. The findings will inform clinical practice, health policy, and future clinical trial design in Taiwan.

---

### 2. Research Objectives

1. **Estimate incidence and prevalence** of ALS in Taiwan from 2016 to 2023, overall and by age, sex, and calendar year.
2. **Model ALSFRS-R-equivalent functional decline** using longitudinal healthcare utilization trajectories derived from outpatient and inpatient claims.
3. **Estimate overall survival** and **time to invasive ventilation** among patients with ALS, and identify associated factors.

---

### 3. Data Sources and Linkage Plan

| Dataset | Description | Use in This Study |
|--------|-------------|-------------------|
| Health-01 | Outpatient care claims | ALS diagnosis, outpatient visits, neurology/rehabilitation/respiratory visits, riluzole prescriptions, NIV equipment/procedures, comorbidities |
| Health-02 | Inpatient care claims | ALS diagnosis, hospitalizations, tracheostomy, invasive mechanical ventilation, gastrostomy, discharge diagnoses, procedures |
| Health-08 | Catastrophic illness registry | Confirmation of ALS catastrophic illness certification, date of certification, validation of claims-based diagnosis |
| Health-10 | Cause of death data | Date of death, underlying and contributing causes of death |
| NHI enrollment/denominator file | Beneficiary enrollment and demographic data | Person-time denominators for incidence and prevalence; age, sex, enrollment dates |

All datasets will be linked by scrambled patient identifier. The study period will be 2016–2023. For incidence estimation, 2016 will serve as a washout period, and incident cases will be identified from 2017–2023. If needed, ICD-9-CM 335.20 will be used for pre-2016 washout to exclude prevalent cases.

---

### 4. Cohort Definition

**Primary ALS cohort:**
- Age ≥20 years at index date (primary analysis; all ages included in sensitivity analysis).
- At least one of the following:
  1. One inpatient discharge diagnosis with ICD-10 G12.21.
  2. Two outpatient claims with ICD-10 G12.21 within 12 months, with at least one claim by a neurologist.
  3. ALS catastrophic illness certification in Health-08.
- Index date: first date on which the above criteria are met.
- Exclusion criteria:
  - Prior ALS diagnosis (ICD-10 G12.21 or ICD-9-CM 335.20) during the washout period.
  - Missing sex or age.
  - Other motor neuron disease or ALS mimic diagnoses if clinically inconsistent (sensitivity analysis).

**Incident cohort:** Patients meeting cohort criteria during 2017–2023 with no prior ALS diagnosis in 2016 washout.  
**Prevalent cohort:** Patients alive with ALS on December 31 of each calendar year.  
**Validation:** The claims-based cohort will be compared with the Health-08 catastrophic illness registry. A strict cohort (catastrophic illness certification only) will be used in sensitivity analyses.

---

### 5. Exposures and Outcomes

**Exposures / Key Covariates:**
- **Riluzole use:** Prescriptions for riluzole (ATC N07XX02) after index date. Time-varying exposure; cumulative defined daily doses and medication possession ratio (MPR) over 6-month intervals.
- **Non-invasive ventilation (NIV):** NHI procedure/equipment codes for non-invasive positive pressure ventilation. Time-varying.
- **Tracheostomy / invasive ventilation:** NHI procedure codes for tracheostomy or prolonged invasive mechanical ventilation. Time-varying.
- **Age at onset:** Age at first ALS diagnosis (proxy for age at onset).
- **Sex:** Male/female.
- **Additional covariates:** Comorbidities (e.g., diabetes, hypertension, COPD, dementia), gastrostomy, rehabilitation use, emergency department visits, hospitalizations.

**Outcomes:**
1. **Incidence and prevalence:**
   - Annual incidence per 100,000 person-years.
   - Annual prevalence per 100,000 mid-year population.
   - Age- and sex-standardized rates using the 2016 Taiwan population.
2. **ALSFRS-R-equivalent functional decline:**
   - Because ALSFRS-R is not available in claims, we will construct a claims-based ALSFRS-R-equivalent score (c-ALSFRS-R) using longitudinal healthcare utilization markers mapped to ALS functional domains:
     - Bulbar: speech therapy, dysphagia-related visits, percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG).
     - Fine motor: occupational therapy, assistive device claims.
     - Gross motor: rehabilitation visits, wheelchair/ambulation-related claims, falls/emergency visits.
     - Respiratory: NIV, respiratory therapy, oxygen, respiratory failure hospitalizations.
   - A pre-specified expert-panel mapping will generate a 0–48 score. In sensitivity analyses, a data-driven latent variable model (e.g., item response theory or latent class mixed model) will be used.
   - Repeated measures will be constructed quarterly from index date.
3. **Overall survival:**
   - Time from index date to death (Health-10) or censoring (end of study period, disenrollment, or December 31, 2023).
   - All-cause mortality and ALS-specific mortality (ALS as underlying cause).
4. **Time to invasive ventilation:**
   - Time from index date to first tracheostomy or initiation of prolonged invasive mechanical ventilation.
   - Death will be treated as a competing event.

---

### 6. Statistical Analysis Plan

**6.1 Incidence and Prevalence**
- Annual incidence: number of new ALS cases / mid-year population at risk, expressed per 100,000 person-years with 95% confidence intervals (Poisson exact).
- Annual prevalence: number of prevalent ALS cases on December 31 / mid-year population, per 100,000.
- Age-sex standardization and Poisson regression to assess trends over time.

**6.2 Overall Survival**
- Kaplan-Meier curves for overall survival from index date.
- Median survival and 5-year survival with 95% CI.
- Cox proportional hazards regression to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) for age, sex, riluzole use, NIV, tracheostomy, and comorbidities. Riluzole, NIV, and tracheostomy will be modeled as time-dependent covariates.
- Proportional hazards assumption checked using Schoenfeld residuals and log(-log) plots.

**6.3 Time to Invasive Ventilation**
- Cumulative incidence function (CIF) with death as a competing event.
- Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard model and cause-specific Cox model.
- Kaplan-Meier will be used for descriptive purposes, recognizing competing risk.

**6.4 Functional Decline (c-ALSFRS-R)**
- Linear mixed-effects models for repeated c-ALSFRS-R measures:
  - Fixed effects: time (months from index), age, sex, riluzole, NIV, tracheostomy, and time-by-covariate interactions.
  - Random effects: random intercept and random slope per patient.
  - Non-linear time trends modeled using restricted cubic splines.
  - Covariance structure: unstructured or spatial power.
- If c-ALSFRS-R is not normally distributed, generalized linear mixed models (e.g., Poisson or negative binomial for utilization counts) will be used.
- Joint modeling of longitudinal c-ALSFRS-R and survival will be considered to account for informative dropout.

**6.5 Sensitivity and Subgroup Analyses**
- Strict cohort using catastrophic illness certification only.
- Exclude patients with other motor neuron diseases or ALS mimics.
- Different washout periods (1 vs. 2 years).
- Subgroups: age <65 vs. ≥65, sex, riluzole users vs. non-users, NIV vs. no NIV, tracheostomy vs. no tracheostomy.
- Multiple imputation for missing covariate data.
- E-value analysis for unmeasured confounding.

**6.6 Sample Size Considerations**
Taiwan’s population is approximately 23.5 million. Assuming an ALS incidence of 1–2 per 100,000 person-years, we expect approximately 250–400 new cases per year, or 1,750–2,800 incident cases over 7 years. Prevalence is expected to be 3–5 per 100,000, yielding several hundred prevalent cases per year. This provides adequate power for survival and longitudinal analyses, with many patients contributing multiple outpatient visits.

---

### 7. Ethical Considerations and Data Security

- The study will be approved by the Institutional Review Board (IRB) of [Institution] and the NHRI data release committee.
- All data will be anonymized and linked using scrambled identifiers.
- Data will be stored on secure, password-protected servers with restricted access.
- No attempt will be made to re-identify individuals.
- Results will be reported in aggregate form only.

---

### 8. Limitations

- Claims data lack direct clinical measures such as ALSFRS-R, FVC, site of onset, and genetic information.
- c-ALSFRS-R is a proxy and may misclassify functional status.
- Diagnostic coding errors and undercoding are possible.
- Riluzole, NIV, and tracheostomy are subject to treatment selection bias and healthy-user effects.
- Socioeconomic status and caregiver support are not directly available.

These limitations will be addressed through strict cohort definitions, validation against the catastrophic illness registry, sensitivity analyses, and cautious interpretation.

---

### 9. Expected Contributions

This study will provide the first comprehensive nationwide estimates of ALS incidence, prevalence, functional decline, and survival in Taiwan. It will clarify the real-world impact of riluzole, NIV, and tracheostomy on disease progression and mortality. The findings will support clinical decision-making, health policy planning, and the design of future ALS registries and clinical trials in Taiwan.

#### Health-01 全民健保處方及治療明細檔_門急診
Years:

**Title:**  
Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Disease Progression, Functional Decline, and Survival in Taiwan: A Nationwide NHIRD-Based Cohort Study

**Data Application to:**  
National Health Research Institutes (NHRI), Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD/NHRID)

**Summary:**  
We propose a retrospective, population-based cohort study using linked NHIRD claims and registry files to describe the epidemiology of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS; ICD-10-CM G12.21) in Taiwan, model an ALSFRS-R-equivalent functional decline trajectory from healthcare utilization patterns, and estimate overall survival and time to invasive ventilation. The study will link Health-01 (outpatient), Health-02 (inpatient), Health-08 (catastrophic illness registry), and Health-10 (cause of death). The results will provide national estimates of ALS incidence and prevalence, real-world prognostic factors, and evidence to inform NHI resource allocation and care planning.

---

## 1. Background

ALS is a progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by motor neuron loss, leading to worsening bulbar, limb, and respiratory function, and ultimately death, most often from respiratory failure. Although ALS is rare, its clinical burden is high because of rapid functional decline, need for multidisciplinary care, non-invasive ventilation (NIV), tracheostomy, and palliative care. Taiwan’s National Health Insurance (NHI) covers more than 99% of the population, and the NHIRD provides a unique opportunity to study ALS at the national level with longitudinal follow-up and linkage to death registration.

ALS is a NHI catastrophic illness in Taiwan, which enhances case ascertainment through the Health-08 catastrophic illness registry. However, the NHIRD does not contain direct clinical measures such as the ALS Functional Rating Scale-Revised (ALSFRS-R). Therefore, we will derive a claims-based ALSFRS-R-equivalent functional burden index using ALS-relevant healthcare utilization trajectories. This approach can capture functional decline indirectly and allows nationwide longitudinal modeling.

The proposed study addresses three unmet needs:  
1. Contemporary national estimates of ALS incidence and prevalence in Taiwan.  
2. A reproducible method to model functional decline using claims data.  
3. Real-world estimates of survival and time to invasive ventilation, accounting for riluzole, NIV, and tracheostomy.

---

## 2. Objectives

1. **Estimate incidence and prevalence** of ALS (ICD-10-CM G12.21) in Taiwan from 2017 to 2023, overall and by age, sex, and calendar year.  
2. **Model ALSFRS-R-equivalent functional decline** using longitudinal healthcare utilization trajectories, including outpatient visits, inpatient admissions, emergency department visits, and ALS-related procedures.  
3. **Estimate overall survival and time to invasive ventilation** from the index date, and evaluate the association with age at onset, sex, riluzole use, NIV, and tracheostomy.

---

## 3. Methods

### 3.1 Design and Data Sources

**Design:** Retrospective, nationwide, population-based cohort study.

**Data period:** 2016–2023, with 2016 used as a washout period and 2017–2023 as the primary study period (or latest available year).

**Data sources and linkage plan:**

| NHRI File | Content | Use in this study |
|---|---|---|
| Health-01 | Outpatient care claims | ALS diagnosis, neurology visits, riluzole prescriptions, rehabilitation, speech/swallowing therapy, NIV-related outpatient care |
| Health-02 | Inpatient claims | ALS diagnosis, hospitalizations, emergency admissions, invasive ventilation, tracheostomy, PEG, respiratory failure, aspiration pneumonia |
| Health-08 | Catastrophic illness registry | High-specificity ALS case ascertainment; certificate date |
| Health-10 | Cause of death data | Date and underlying cause of death for survival analysis |

All files will be linked by NHRI-encrypted beneficiary identifier, birth date, and sex. No attempt will be made to re-identify patients. For incidence and prevalence denominators, we will use NHRI beneficiary enrollment files if available, or NHI annual enrollment statistics and mid-year population denominators.

---

### 3.2 Cohort Definition

**Source population:** All NHI beneficiaries in Taiwan during the study period.

**ALS case definition:**  
Primary definition:  
- At least one outpatient or inpatient claim with ICD-10-CM **G12.21** (amyotrophic lateral sclerosis), **and**  
- Health-08 catastrophic illness registration for ALS/motor neuron disease.

Secondary definition:  
- At least two outpatient G12.21 diagnoses separated by ≥30 days, or  
- At least one inpatient discharge diagnosis of G12.21, with at least one neurology-related visit.

**Index date:** Earliest date of the first G12.21 claim or Health-08 ALS certificate date.

**Incident case:** First G12.21 claim after a washout period with no G12.21 diagnosis in the prior 12 months (primary) or 24 months (sensitivity analysis). Patients with prevalent ALS before the washout period will be excluded from incidence analyses.

**Inclusion criteria:**  
- Age ≥20 years at index date for the main analysis.  
- Continuous NHI enrollment for at least 6 months before index date for covariate assessment.

**Exclusion criteria:**  
- Prevalent ALS before the study period.  
- Missing sex or birth date.  
- No follow-up after index date for progression analyses.

**Prevalent case:** Any patient with a G12.21 diagnosis or Health-08 ALS registration who is alive at the mid-year prevalence date.

---

### 3.3 Exposures

| Exposure | Definition |
|---|---|
| Age at onset | Age at index date (proxy for age at onset) |
| Sex | Male/female from NHRI demographic files |
| Riluzole use | Prescription claims for riluzole (ATC N07XX02). Defined as ever/never, current/former/never, cumulative defined daily dose (DDD), and medication possession ratio (MPR) |
| NIV | Procedure or order codes for non-invasive positive pressure ventilation or home respiratory care from Health-01/Health-02 |
| Tracheostomy | Procedure code for tracheostomy from Health-02 |
| Invasive ventilation | Procedure codes for endotracheal intubation and invasive mechanical ventilation from Health-02 |

Riluzole, NIV, and tracheostomy will be modeled as time-varying exposures to avoid immortal time bias. Landmark analyses at 3, 6, and 12 months will be performed as sensitivity analyses.

---

### 3.4 Outcomes

**Primary outcomes:**

1. **Incidence and prevalence**  
   - Annual incidence rate per 100,000 person-years.  
   - Annual prevalence per 100,000 mid-year population.  
   - Age- and sex-standardized to the 2020 Taiwan population.

2. **ALSFRS-R-equivalent functional decline**  
   Because ALSFRS-R is not directly available in NHIRD, we will derive a claims-based functional decline index (cALSFRS-R) mapped to the 12 ALSFRS-R domains:

| ALSFRS-R Domain | Claims-Based Proxy |
|---|---|
| Speech | Speech therapy, dysarthria visits, communication device |
| Salivation | Sialorrhea treatment, botulinum toxin, outpatient visits |
| Swallowing | Dysphagia diagnosis, swallowing study, PEG insertion, aspiration pneumonia |
| Handwriting | Occupational therapy, hand weakness visits, assistive device |
| Cutting food/handling utensils | OT, PEG, home care |
| Dressing/hygiene | OT, home care |
| Turning in bed | Home care, fall-related hospitalization |
| Walking | Wheelchair, walker, cane, rehabilitation, fall injury |
| Climbing stairs | Same as walking |
| Dyspnea | Oxygen, NIV, respiratory failure, ER visit |
| Orthopnea | NIV, sleep study, respiratory failure |
| Respiratory insufficiency | NIV, tracheostomy, invasive ventilation, ICU admission |

Each domain will be scored 0–4 (higher = better function) based on event presence and severity. The sum yields a 0–48 cALSFRS-R-equivalent score. Scores will be calculated quarterly and carried forward if no new events occur. The index will be validated against clinical ALSFRS-R in a collaborating hospital subset if permitted.

3. **Overall survival**  
   - Time from index date to death from any cause (Health-10).  
   - Censored at disenrollment, end of study, or last contact.

4. **Time to invasive ventilation**  
   - Time from index date to first tracheostomy or invasive mechanical ventilation.  
   - Death will be treated as a competing risk.

**Secondary outcomes:**  
- Time to NIV initiation.  
- Cause-specific survival (ALS-related death, respiratory failure, other causes).  
- Hospitalization for aspiration pneumonia or respiratory failure.  
- Healthcare utilization trajectories: quarterly counts of outpatient visits, ED visits, and hospitalizations.

---

### 3.5 Covariates

Covariates will be measured at baseline or as time-varying where appropriate:

- Age at index date (proxy for age at onset).
- Sex.
- Riluzole use (time-varying).
- NIV initiation (time-varying).
- Tracheostomy (time-varying or outcome).
- Charlson Comorbidity Index and individual comorbidities (diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, COPD, dementia, depression).
- Baseline healthcare utilization (outpatient visits, hospitalizations in the prior year).
- Year of diagnosis.
- Hospital level and physician specialty (neurology vs. non-neurology).
- Geographic region or urbanization if available.

---

## 4. Statistical Plan

### 4.1 Incidence and Prevalence

- **Incidence rate:** Number of incident ALS cases divided by total person-years at risk, expressed per 100,000 person-years.  
- **Prevalence:** Number of alive ALS cases at mid-year divided by mid-year NHI population, per 100,000.  
- **Confidence intervals:** Poisson exact or normal approximation.  
- **Trend analysis:** Poisson regression with calendar year, age group, and sex.  
- **Standardization:** Direct standardization to the 2020 Taiwan population.

### 4.2 ALSFRS-R-Equivalent Functional Decline

We will use **mixed-effects models** for longitudinal data.

**Primary model:**

\[
Y_{it} = \beta_0 + \beta_1 t + \beta_2 \text{age}_i + \beta_3 \text{sex}_i + \beta_4 \text{riluzole}_{it} + \beta_5 \text{NIV}_{it} + \beta_6 \text{tracheostomy}_{it} + \beta_7 \text{CCI}_i + b_{0i} + b_{1i}t + \varepsilon_{it}
\]

Where:  
- \(Y_{it}\) = cALSFRS-R-equivalent score for patient \(i\) at time \(t\).  
- \(t\) = time since index date in years.  
- \(b_{0i}\) and \(b_{1i}\) = random intercept and random slope.  
- \(\varepsilon_{it}\) = residual error.

We will use restricted cubic splines for time to capture nonlinear decline. For count outcomes (visits, hospitalizations), negative binomial mixed models will be used. For binary outcomes (e.g., PEG, NIV), generalized linear mixed models with logit link will be used.

**Trajectory classes:** Latent class mixed models will identify slow, intermediate, and rapid progressors. Model selection will use BIC, entropy, and clinical interpretability.

**Informative dropout:** Because death is common, joint modeling of longitudinal cALSFRS-R and survival will be performed as a sensitivity analysis.

### 4.3 Survival and Time to Invasive Ventilation

- **Kaplan-Meier curves** for overall survival, stratified by riluzole, NIV, tracheostomy, age group, and sex.  
- **Cox proportional hazards regression** with time-varying covariates for riluzole, NIV, and tracheostomy.  
- **Proportional hazards assumption** checked with Schoenfeld residuals; if violated, time-varying coefficients or restricted mean survival time (RMST) will be used.  
- **Competing risk analysis** for time to invasive ventilation: cumulative incidence function, cause-specific Cox, and Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models. Death will be treated as a competing event.  
- **Landmark analysis** at 3, 6, and 12 months to avoid immortal time bias for NIV and tracheostomy.  
- **Subgroup analyses:** age <60 vs. ≥60, sex, bulbar vs. limb onset (if proxy available), riluzole users vs. non-users, NIV users vs. non-users.

### 4.4 Sensitivity and Validation Analyses

- Primary vs. secondary ALS case definitions.
- 12-month vs. 24-month washout.
- Excluding patients with only one G12.21 claim.
- Different code sets for NIV/invasive ventilation.
- Excluding early deaths (<30 days after index).
- Validation of cALSFRS-R against clinical ALSFRS-R in a subset of patients from collaborating hospitals (if IRB and data linkage permit).
- Missing data will be handled with multiple imputation if needed; claims data are otherwise complete.

### 4.5 Sample Size and Power

Taiwan’s population is approximately 23 million. With an estimated ALS incidence of 1.5–2.5 per 100,000 person-years, we expect approximately 2,500–3,500 incident cases over 7 years and 1,000–2,000 prevalent cases. This provides >80% power to detect hazard ratios of 1.25–1.30 for common exposures with 50% mortality. Power will be lower for rare subgroups and interactions.

---

## 5. Ethical Considerations and Data Security

- The study will use de-identified NHRI data and will comply with NHRI data governance and IRB requirements.
- No attempt will be made to re-identify individuals.
- Data will be stored on secure, access-controlled servers.
- Results will be reported in aggregate form only.

---

## 6. Limitations

- NHIRD lacks direct ALSFRS-R measurements; the cALSFRS-R is a proxy and may misclassify functional status.
- Claims data may undercode NIV, tracheostomy, and riluzole adherence.
- Age at index date is a proxy for age at onset.
- Unmeasured confounders such as socioeconomic status, caregiver support, and patient preferences may influence NIV/tracheostomy use.
- Cause of death may be incomplete or inaccurate.
- Competing risks and informative dropout are important in ALS and will be addressed with joint models and competing risk methods.

---

## 7. Expected Contributions

This study will provide the most comprehensive nationwide description of ALS in Taiwan to date. It will:  
- Generate contemporary incidence and prevalence estimates.  
- Develop a reproducible claims-based method to model ALS functional decline.  
- Quantify real-world survival and time to invasive ventilation.  
- Evaluate the association of riluzole, NIV, and tracheostomy with outcomes.  
- Inform NHI policy, clinical care pathways, and resource planning for ALS in Taiwan.

---

# NHRI Data Application Research Proposal

## Project Title
**Disease Progression, Functional Decline, and Survival in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis: A Population-Based Cohort Study Using the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD)**

---

## 1. Summary

Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a rapidly progressive, universally fatal neurodegenerative disease with a median survival of 2–5 years from symptom onset. Taiwan's National Health Insurance (NHI) system, covering >99% of the population, offers a unique opportunity to characterize the epidemiology and clinical trajectory of ALS at a national scale. Leveraging four linked NHRI datasets — Health-01 (ambulatory care), Health-02 (inpatient claims), Health-08 (catastrophic illness registry), and Health-10 (cause of death) — this study will (1) estimate the incidence and prevalence of ALS (ICD-10-CM G12.21), (2) construct and validate ALSFRS-R–equivalent functional decline trajectories from longitudinal healthcare utilization, and (3) estimate overall survival and time to invasive ventilation, with riluzole use, non-invasive ventilation (NIV), and tracheostomy as key exposures. Findings will inform national ALS care policy, resource allocation for respiratory support, and real-world evidence on riluzole effectiveness in an East Asian population.

---

## 2. Background

### 2.1 Disease burden
ALS is characterized by the degeneration of upper and lower motor neurons, leading to progressive muscle weakness, bulbar dysfunction, respiratory failure, and death. Global incidence is estimated at 1.5–2.5 per 100,000 person-years and prevalence at 5–8 per 100,000, with considerable geographic variation. East Asian populations, including Taiwan, remain underrepresented in ALS epidemiologic and health-services research.

### 2.2 Functional assessment and claims-based proxies
The ALS Functional Rating Scale–Revised (ALSFRS-R) is the gold-standard clinical measure of disease progression but is not systematically recorded in claims data. Functional decline in ALS nonetheless produces a highly stereotyped cascade of healthcare events — accelerating neurology visits, gastrostomy placement, home respiratory care, NIV initiation, emergency presentations for dyspnea or falls, and eventual hospitalization. These utilization patterns can plausibly serve as **claims-based surrogates** for ALSFRS-R domains, an approach validated in other neurodegenerative diseases but not yet formally established in ALS.

### 2.3 Survival and respiratory interventions
Median survival from diagnosis is approximately 24–36 months. NIV extends survival and improves quality of life; invasive ventilation via tracheostomy is offered variably across cultures and health systems, with Taiwan having one of the world's highest long-term mechanical ventilation utilization rates. Real-world estimates of time to NIV and tracheostomy, and their association with survival, are needed.

### 2.4 Rationale
The NHIRD provides a complete, longitudinally linkable record of the entire Taiwanese ALS population, including catastrophic illness certification (which ALS qualifies for), cause-of-death data, and all respiratory care utilization. This enables the first nationally representative, ICD-10–era characterization of ALS disease progression in Taiwan.

---

## 3. Study Objectives

**Primary objective 1 — Epidemiology**
Estimate the annual incidence and point prevalence of ALS in Taiwan (2016–2023), overall and stratified by age group, sex, and region.

**Primary objective 2 — Functional decline modeling**
Derive claims-based ALSFRS-R–equivalent trajectories from longitudinal healthcare utilization and identify distinct functional decline phenotypes.

**Primary objective 3 — Survival and respiratory outcomes**
Estimate overall survival from diagnosis and time to (a) NIV initiation and (b) invasive ventilation (tracheostomy/prolonged mechanical ventilation), and identify their determinants.

**Secondary exploratory objectives**
- Quantify real-world riluzole persistence and its association with survival and time to respiratory support.
- Characterize healthcare costs and end-of-life care intensity.

---

## 4. Materials and Methods

### 4.1 Data sources and linkage

| Dataset | Content | Role in analysis |
|---|---|---|
| **Health-01** | Ambulatory care claims (diagnoses, prescriptions, procedures) | Cohort identification; riluzole exposure; outpatient utilization trajectory |
| **Health-02** | Inpatient claims (admissions, procedures, ventilation) | NIV/tracheostomy identification; inpatient utilization trajectory; outcome ascertainment |
| **Health-08** | Catastrophic illness registry | ALS certification date; validation of diagnosis; index date confirmation |
| **Health-10** | Cause-of-death file | All-cause and ALS-specific mortality; censoring |

Linkage will be performed by NHRI using de-identified unique personal identifiers. All analyses will use the encrypted, researcher-accessible version. Data extraction will be restricted to fields required for cohort definition, exposure, outcome, and covariate ascertainment (minimal necessary dataset principle).

### 4.2 Cohort definition

**Inclusion criteria**
1. At least one claim with a principal or secondary diagnosis of **ICD-10-CM G12.21** (amyotrophic lateral sclerosis) between **1 January 2016 and 31 December 2023**.
2. Diagnosis confirmed by either:
   - ≥2 outpatient visits with G12.21 on separate dates, **or**
   - ≥1 inpatient admission with G12.21 as a discharge diagnosis, **or**
   - Registration in the **catastrophic illness registry (Health-08)** for ALS.
3. Continuous NHI enrollment for ≥12 months before the index date (baseline covariate window).
4. Age ≥20 years at index date.

**Exclusion criteria**
1. Any G12.21 or legacy ICD-9-CM 335.20 code in the 12 months before index date (to exclude prevalent cases misclassified as incident).
2. Concurrent diagnosis of other motor neuron diseases (G12.0, G12.1, G12.8) or secondary ALS-like syndromes.
3. Prior tracheostomy or chronic mechanical ventilation (≥21 days) before index date (for the respiratory outcome subanalysis).

**Index date**: the earlier of (a) the first qualifying G12.21 claim or (b) the ALS catastrophic illness certification date.

**Prevalent cohort**: all patients with ≥1 qualifying G12.21 claim in a given calendar year (numerator), divided by mid-year NHI enrollees (denominator).

### 4.3 Exposure variables

| Exposure | Operational definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Riluzole** | Prescription of riluzole (ATC N07XX02) ≥28 cumulative defined daily doses; modeled as time-varying (current/former/never) | Health-01 |
| **NIV** | Billing codes for non-invasive ventilation (e.g., BiPAP/CPAP device rental or respiratory care procedures) on ≥2 occasions | Health-01, Health-02 |
| **Tracheostomy / IMV** | Inpatient procedure codes for tracheostomy (e.g., 47011B, 47012B) or prolonged mechanical ventilation ≥21 days | Health-02 |
| **Gastrostomy (PEG)** | Procedure codes for percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy | Health-02 |

### 4.4 Outcome variables

1. **Incidence / prevalence** — person-year incidence with 95% CI, age–sex standardized to the 2020 Taiwan population.
2. **Functional decline trajectory** — a composite longitudinal index constructed from quarterly counts of: outpatient visits, inpatient days, emergency department visits, home nursing visits, respiratory therapy sessions, and gastrostomy/respiratory procedure events. This index will be mapped to an ALSFRS-R–equivalent score using (a) content validity mapping against published domain structures and (b) internal validation against a small clinically annotated chart-review subset (if available through collaborating hospitals via IRB-approved sub-study).
3. **Overall survival** — time from index date to death (any cause, from Health-10) or censoring (deregistration, 31 December 2023).
4. **Time to invasive ventilation** — time from index date to first tracheostomy or prolonged MV event (deaths before event treated as competing risk).

### 4.5 Covariates

- Age at index/onset
- Sex
- Region of residence (urbanization level)
- Charlson Comorbidity Index (from Health-01/02)
- Bulbar vs. limb onset (proxied by early speech/swallowing-related claims: dysarthria, dysphagia, PEG timing)
- Riluzole use (as above)
- NIV and tracheostomy (as time-varying exposures in survival models)
- Baseline healthcare utilization intensity (prior-year visits)
- Socioeconomic proxies (copayment category, occupational insurance tier)

---

## 5. Statistical Analysis Plan

### 5.1 Descriptive epidemiology
Annual incidence and prevalence calculated with exact Poisson 95% CIs; direct standardization to the 2020 Taiwan census population. Trends tested with Poisson regression and joinpoint analysis.

### 5.2 Functional decline modeling
- **Mixed-effects models**: linear mixed models (or generalized linear mixed models with a Poisson/log link for count data) with random intercepts and slopes for each patient, modeling the quarterly composite utilization index over time from index date. Fixed effects: time, age, sex, riluzole, NIV, comorbidity burden, and time×covariate interactions.
- **Latent class growth analysis (LCGA) / group-based trajectory modeling**: to identify 3–5 distinct functional decline phenotypes (e.g., rapid, intermediate, slow decliners). Model selection by BIC, entropy, and clinical interpretability.
- **Validation**: internal cross-validation; sensitivity analysis with alternative index definitions.

### 5.3 Survival analysis
- **Kaplan-Meier** curves for overall survival and time to invasive ventilation, stratified by riluzole use, NIV use, age group, and decline phenotype (landmark analysis at 6 months to avoid immortal time bias).
- **Cox proportional hazards regression** with time-varying covariates for riluzole, NIV, and tracheostomy. Proportional hazards assumption verified by Schoenfeld residuals; if violated, use time-varying coefficients or restricted mean survival time (RMST).
- **Competing-risk analysis (Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards)** for time to invasive ventilation, treating death as a competing event.
- **Immortal time bias mitigation**: landmark analysis and time-dependent Cox models; sensitivity analysis with new-user active-comparator design for riluzole.
- **Propensity score methods** (IPTW or matching) for riluzole and NIV comparisons, adjusting for measured confounders.

### 5.4 Subgroup and sensitivity analyses
- By sex, age (<65 vs. ≥65), bulbar vs. limb onset, and urbanization.
- Excluding patients with <6 months of follow-up.
- Using catastrophic illness certification alone as the cohort definition (registry-based sensitivity analysis).
- Cause-specific mortality (ALS-related deaths, ICD-10 G12.21 as underlying cause in Health-10).

### 5.5 Power considerations
Based on an assumed Taiwanese ALS incidence of 1.5 per 100,000 and an 8-year observation window across ~23 million NHI enrollees, we anticipate approximately 2,500–3,500 incident cases — sufficient to detect hazard ratios of ≥1.4 for riluzole/NIV effects on survival at 80% power (α=0.05, two-sided) and to support LCGA with ≥5 trajectory classes.

### 5.6 Software
SAS 9.4 / R 4.3 (packages: `survival`, `cmprsk`, `lme4`, `lcmm`, `traj`, `MatchIt`). All code and analytic decisions will be preregistered and version-controlled.

---

## 6. Ethical Considerations and Data Governance

- The study uses de-identified secondary data; exemption from informed consent will be sought from the institutional IRB per Taiwan's Human Subjects Research Act.
- All analyses will be conducted in the NHRI-designated secure remote analysis environment; no individual-level data will leave the platform.
- Data will be used solely for the stated research objectives; results will be reported only in aggregate form to prevent re-identification.
- Compliance with the Personal Data Protection Act and NHRI data-use agreement.

---

## 7. Limitations

1. Claims-based functional proxies are not equivalent to ALSFRS-R; validation against a clinical sub-cohort is a priority.
2. Onset date is approximated by diagnosis/certification date; true symptom onset typically precedes by 10–12 months.
3. Riluzole exposure is prescription-based, not adherence-verified.
4. NIV and tracheostomy coding may vary across hospitals; sensitivity analyses will address misclassification.
5. Unmeasured confounders (genetics, socioeconomic status, caregiver support) may bias treatment-effect estimates; propensity methods mitigate but do not eliminate this.

---

- **First national, ICD-10–era epidemiologic profile of ALS in Taiwan.**
- **A validated claims-based functional trajectory framework** transferable to other neurodegenerative diseases and other NHI-type systems.
- **Real-world evidence on riluzole, NIV, and tracheostomy** to guide Taiwan NHI reimbursement and respiratory care policy.

# Data Application Research Proposal to the National Health Research Institutes (NHRI) Health and Welfare Data Science Center (HWDC)

**Title:** Disease Progression, Functional Decline, and Survival in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis: A Nationwide Population-Based Cohort Study Using the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD)

**Short title:** ALS-NHIRD Taiwan

**Proposed study period:** 1 January 2016 – 31 December 2023 (with 2016 as diagnostic wash-in and 2017–2022 as the incident cohort window)

**Version:** 1.0 (application draft)

---

## 1. Summary

Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a uniformly fatal motor neuron disease with a median survival of 2–4 years from symptom onset and no curative therapy. Taiwan offers a unique opportunity to characterise the natural history of ALS at national scale: the National Health Insurance (NHI) programme covers >99% of the population, and ALS is one of the diseases for which patients are entitled to a **catastrophic illness certificate (重大傷病證明)**, which is both a robust case-ascertainment source and a powerful economic incentive for registration.

We propose to assemble a nationwide, population-based ALS cohort using ICD-10-CM code **G12.21** across **Health-01 (outpatient), Health-02 (inpatient), Health-08 (catastrophic illness registry), and Health-10 (cause-of-death)** files, with deterministic person-level linkage via the encrypted beneficiary identifier. The study has three aims: (1) to estimate the contemporary incidence and prevalence of ALS in Taiwan and their temporal, age-, sex-, and region-specific trends; (2) to derive and validate a claims-based ALSFRS-R-equivalent functional index from longitudinal healthcare-utilisation trajectories, and to model individual functional decline trajectories and their determinants; and (3) to estimate overall survival and time to invasive ventilation (tracheostomy / ventilator-dependent status), accounting for death as a competing risk, and to quantify the associations of riluzole and non-invasive ventilation (NIV) with these outcomes.

The outputs will inform prognostic counselling, long-term ventilation and home-care resource planning, and health-technology assessment for emerging ALS therapies in Taiwan.

---

## 2. Background and Significance

### 2.1 Disease burden and the Asian context
ALS incidence in European and North American populations is 2–3 per 100,000 person-years, with a male-to-female ratio of approximately 1.3–1.5:1 and a median age of onset of 60–65 years. Asian population-based estimates are systematically lower (0.6–1.5 per 100,000), and East Asian cohorts report a younger age of onset and a lower frequency of *C9orf72* expansions than Caucasian cohorts. Whether this reflects true biological differences, diagnostic access, or case ascertainment is unresolved. Taiwanese data derived from the NHIRD have reported age-standardised incidence estimates in the range of approximately 1.0–1.9 per 100,000 person-years when the catastrophic illness registry is used for ascertainment, but estimates have varied substantially by case definition and study period, and most predate the ICD-10-CM transition of the NHI claims system (1 January 2016).

### 2.2 The functional decline measurement gap
The ALS Functional Rating Scale–Revised (ALSFRS-R) is the accepted primary outcome for functional decline in ALS trials and clinics, declining on average by ~1 point per month. It is recorded in hospital charts but **not available in claims data**. As a result, nationwide ALS studies have been restricted to crude endpoints (death, tracheostomy, hospitalisation) and cannot model the trajectory that patients and clinicians actually care about. A validated claims-based proxy for the ALSFRS-R would unlock a national-scale description of progression phenotypes (rapid vs. slow progressors), allow identification of determinants of decline rate, provide historical benchmarks for single-arm trial design, and enable pharmacoepidemiological evaluation of riluzole or future therapies on functional endpoints.

### 2.3 The Taiwanese ventilation paradigm
The proportion of ALS patients receiving tracheostomy and long-term invasive mechanical ventilation in Taiwan is substantially higher than in Western cohorts — a pattern shared with Japan and Korea and driven by NHI coverage of ventilator-dependent care, family decision-making norms, and the absence of a hospice-first default. Survival estimates imported from European or North American series are therefore **not transportable** to Taiwan, and time-to-ventilation is a decision-relevant, culturally specific endpoint in its own right. How NIV, which is NHI-reimbursed and increasingly used, modifies the timing of invasive ventilation and survival in the Taiwanese context is unknown.

### 2.4 Significance
This project will deliver: (i) the most contemporary, nationally complete estimate of ALS epidemiology in Taiwan; (ii) a validated, reusable claims-based functional index and an open phenotype definition for the Taiwanese ALS population; (iii) prognostic models for survival and ventilation timing; and (iv) the analytic scaffolding for a future national ALS registry and for real-world evidence generation on new ALS therapies.

---

## 3. Specific Aims

**Aim 1 — Epidemiology.** To estimate the annual incidence (2017–2022) and the annual point prevalence (2016–2023) of ALS in Taiwan overall and by age, sex, region, and urbanisation level; to quantify temporal trends using age–period–cohort modelling; and to estimate case-ascertainment completeness by capture–recapture using the claims definition and the catastrophic illness registry as two independent sources.

**Aim 2 — Functional decline.** To derive a claims-based ALSFRS-R-equivalent index (the **Claims-based ALS Functional Index, cAFI**) from longitudinal healthcare-utilisation and procedure markers, to validate it against chart-recorded ALSFRS-R in a hospital sub-cohort, and to model individual-level functional trajectories using linear mixed-effects and latent-class growth models; to identify baseline and time-varying determinants of rapid decline.

**Aim 3 — Survival and ventilation.** To estimate overall survival from index diagnosis and from first ALS-related symptom code; to estimate the cumulative incidence of invasive ventilation (tracheostomy or registration as a ventilator-dependent patient) treating death as a competing risk; and to estimate the association of riluzole use and NIV initiation with both outcomes using time-varying exposure models that address immortal-time and confounding-by-indication bias.

## 5. Cohort Definition

### 5.1 Case ascertainment (ALS case definition)
A patient is classified as an ALS case if **either** of the following is met:

- **(A) Catastrophic illness registry definition (primary, high-specificity):** a record in Health-08 for the ALS/motor neuron disease catastrophic illness category, with a certification date within the study period; **or**
- **(B) Claims-based definition (high-sensitivity):** ≥1 inpatient claim **or** ≥2 outpatient claims with ICD-10-CM **G12.21** (amyotrophic lateral sclerosis) in the primary or secondary diagnostic fields, with at least one such claim associated with a neurology, rehabilitation, or physical medicine and rehabilitation specialty visit, occurring within a 365-day window.

For 2016 index dates arising in the wash-in period, the ICD-9-CM equivalent code **335.20** will be accepted. From 1 January 2017 onward, ICD-10-CM codes only.

A case is confirmed as incident only if there is **no** qualifying ALS code or catastrophic illness certificate in the 12 months preceding the index date (washout). Cases whose first qualifying evidence falls in 2016 are designated prevalent and excluded from incidence estimation but retained in the prevalence cohort.

### 5.2 Anatomical-site proxy and symptom onset
Because claims data contain no date of symptom onset or site of onset, we will construct:

- **Symptom-onset proxy:** the earliest date of an ALS-related symptom code in the 24 months preceding the index date, drawn from bulbar markers (dysarthria R47.1, dysphagia R13.1, sialorrhoea, unintentional weight loss R63.4), limb markers (muscle weakness M62.81, atrophy M62.50, fasciculation R25.3, gait abnormality R26.2), and respiratory markers (dyspnoea R06.0, orthopnoea, respiratory failure J96.x). Where available, the catastrophic illness certification also carries diagnostic information that will be used to refine the date.
- **Diagnostic delay** = index date − symptom-onset proxy.
- **Bulbar-predominant proxy** = bulbar symptom code precedes any limb symptom code.

This proxy will be validated against chart-recorded onset in the hospital sub-cohort (Aim 2).

### 5.3 Index date and follow-up
- **Index date** = the earlier of (i) the ALS catastrophic illness certification date and (ii) the first qualifying ALS claim.
- **Follow-up** begins at index and ends at the earliest of death, the end of the study period (31 December 2023), a gap in NHI enrolment exceeding 90 days, or the outcome-specific censoring date. Because NHI is a single-payer system with near-universal coverage, attrition other than death is expected to be minimal (primarily emigration).

### 5.4 Inclusion and exclusion criteria

**Inclusion**
1. Qualifying ALS case definition met (5.1).
2. Age ≥20 years at index date.
3. Continuous NHI enrolment for ≥12 months prior to index (to permit comorbidity and prodrome ascertainment), except for the small number of patients whose ALS onset coincides with enrolment, who will be retained in sensitivity analyses.
4. At least 30 days of follow-up, to permit baseline covariate assignment (retained in sensitivity analyses).

**Exclusion**
1. Alternative or competing motor neuron disease diagnoses recorded in the 12 months before index that preclude an ALS classification (e.g., spinal muscular atrophy, hereditary spastic paraplegia, primary lateral sclerosis where coded separately).
2. Strong ALS-mimic diagnoses recorded within 12 months and never subsequently accompanied by a maintained ALS diagnosis (e.g., cervical spondylotic myelopathy, multifocal motor neuropathy, myasthenia gravis, inflammatory myopathy, hyperthyroid myopathy).
3. A single transient ALS code with no further ALS code or certification within 365 days ("one-code-only" cases), excluded from the primary analysis and examined in a sensitivity analysis.
4. For the invasive-ventilation outcome only: pre-existing home mechanical ventilation, tracheostomy, or ventilator-dependent status before the index date (these patients are retained in the survival analysis, with ventilation outcome modelling restricted to those at risk).

### 5.5 Comparator and denominator populations
- **Incidence denominators:** mid-year person-time at risk stratified by age (5-year bands), sex, and calendar year, derived from the enrolment/beneficiary file (or published NHIA statistics if that file is not granted).
- **Prevalence denominators:** the same mid-year population, with point prevalence computed on 31 December of each year.
- **Internal reference for trajectory modelling:** patients with ALS contribute their own longitudinal observations; no external reference cohort is required for the trajectory and survival aims.

### 5.6 Hospital validation sub-cohort (Aim 2)
With separate institutional review board approval at 2–3 participating tertiary ALS clinics, approximately 500–800 patients with chart-documented ALSFRS-R measurements (typically 3-monthly) will be identified, along with date of symptom onset, site of onset, forced vital capacity where available, and ALSFRS-R at each visit. These records will be de-identified, encrypted with the same HWDC linkage key, and linked within the secure environment. This sub-cohort serves exclusively to **derive and validate** the cAFI and the onset proxy; it is not used for the primary epidemiological estimates.

## 6. Exposures, Covariates, and Outcomes

### 6.1 Primary exposures
| Exposure | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Riluzole** | Any dispensing of riluzole identified from drug-order detail fields. Modelled as (a) ever/never, (b) cumulative defined daily doses (cDDD), (c) time-varying current use (dispensing date + expected supply duration, with a 30-day grace period), and (d) adherence measured by proportion of days covered (PDC) over successive 6-month windows. |
| **Non-invasive ventilation (NIV)** | Initiation of NIV identified from NHI procedure and special-material codes for bi-level positive airway pressure and non-invasive ventilatory support, corroborated by home respiratory care claims. Date of first NIV dispensing/setup is the exposure date. |
| **Invasive ventilation** | Tracheostomy procedure code, or registration in the NHI ventilator-dependent patient programme, or ≥21 consecutive days of invasive mechanical ventilation (Health-02 ventilation fields). |

### 6.2 Covariates
- **Demographic:** age at index (and age at symptom-onset proxy, by subtracting diagnostic delay), sex, region (NHI branch/administrative region), urbanisation level of residence, and area-level socioeconomic proxies available within HWDC rules.
- **Clinical:** bulbar-predominant vs. limb-predominant proxy at presentation; diagnostic delay (log-transformed); symptom-onset proxy to index interval; Charlson–Deyo comorbidity index and individual comorbidities (dementia/frontotemporal disease, diabetes, hypertension, chronic respiratory disease, chronic kidney disease, cancer) derived from 12-month look-back; baseline pneumonia or respiratory failure within 90 days of index; baseline weight-loss and nutritional codes.
- **Care delivery:** treating facility accreditation level and ownership, treating physician specialty (neurology vs. other), continuity of neurology care (proportion of ALS-related visits with a neurologist), hospital ALS case volume (facility-level, derived from the cohort), and initial treatment setting (outpatient vs. admitted at index).
- **Co-interventions (time-varying):** percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG), NIV, tracheostomy, home nursing utilisation, hospice enrolment, riluzole.
- **Socioeconomic proxy:** catastrophic illness copayment exemption status and any low-income household registration flag, if released.
