| # | Outcome | Operational definition |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Incident ALS** | First qualifying ALS evidence with 12-month ALS-free washout |
| 2 | **Prevalent ALS** | Any qualifying ALS evidence and alive/enrolled on 31 December of the year |
| 3 | **Claims-based ALS Functional Index (cAFI)** | Composite 0–48 index (Section 7.2 and Table below), computed in successive 90-day windows |
| 4 | **All-cause death** | Date of death from Health-10 (primary) supplemented by NHI disenrolment-for-death flags; cause-specific death from Health-10 underlying cause |
| 5 | **Invasive ventilation** | Tracheostomy, ventilator-dependent registration, or ≥21 consecutive invasive ventilation days, whichever first |
| 6 | **NIV initiation** | First NIV setup (intermediate outcome) |
| 7 | **ALS-related hospitalisation** | First inpatient admission with ALS as primary or secondary diagnosis (secondary outcome; healthcare-utilisation endpoint) |

## 7. Statistical Analysis Plan

### 7.1 Aim 1 — Incidence and prevalence

**Incidence.** Annual incidence rates will be computed as the number of incident cases divided by person-time at risk, overall and stratified by sex, 5-year age band, region, and urbanisation. Rates will be **age-standardised** to the WHO 2000 world population and to the 2020 Taiwan population, with 95% confidence intervals from the Poisson distribution (or exact methods for small strata). Trends will be assessed with:

- Poisson and negative-binomial regression with log person-time offset, including calendar year; over-dispersion assessed and negative-binomial used where indicated;
- **Age–period–cohort (APC) modelling** using the intrinsic estimator or a spline-based APC model to separate period and cohort effects, reported with sensitivity to the identification constraint;
- **Joinpoint regression** for detection of inflection points in the incidence trend.

**Prevalence.** Point prevalence on 31 December of each year (numerator: prevalent cases confirmed alive and enrolled; denominator: mid-year population), age-standardised as above. Period prevalence (any ALS claim within the calendar year) will be reported as a secondary measure to permit comparison with registry-based European estimates.

**Completeness.** Two-source **capture–recapture** analysis with the claims definition (Source A) and the catastrophic illness registry (Source B); the Chapman estimator with log-linear modelling for dependence between sources will be used to estimate the number of undetected cases and the ascertainment-corrected incidence.

### 7.2 Aim 2 — Derivation and validation of the Claims-based ALS Functional Index (cAFI)

**Construct.** The cAFI mirrors the domain structure of the ALSFRS-R, with each of five domains scored 0–4 and summed to a 0–48 scale (higher = better function):

| Domain (ALSFRS-R analogue) | Claims markers (90-day window) |
|---|---|
| **Bulbar** | Dysarthria/dysphagia/sialorrhoea codes; speech or swallowing therapy; nutritional counselling; PEG insertion; weight-loss codes |
| **Fine motor** | Hand weakness/atrophy codes; occupational therapy; assistive-device or splint claims |
| **Gross motor** | Gait abnormality codes; falls; wheelchair or walking-aid reimbursement claims; home-care or long-term-care service claims |
| **Respiratory** | Dyspnoea/orthopnoea codes; NIV initiation or continuation; oxygen claims; respiratory failure and pneumonia admissions; ICU admission |
| **Global function / service intensity** | ALS-related outpatient visit frequency; ALS-related admissions and length of stay; emergency department visits; hospice enrolment |

**Derivation and validation.** Domain weights will be estimated by regressing concurrent chart-recorded ALSFRS-R on the 90-day claims markers in the hospital sub-cohort, using: (i) a constrained linear mixed model with monotonicity imposed on markers (more utilisation of a marker type implies worse function); (ii) an item-response-theory (graded-response) model treating the cAFI markers as indicators of a latent functional trait; and (iii) gradient-boosted regression as a non-parametric benchmark. Model selection will be by cross-validated RMSE and calibration. Performance will be reported as: agreement with concurrent ALSFRS-R (intraclass correlation, Bland–Altman limits of agreement), discrimination for a ≥5-point 3-month decline (AUROC), responsiveness (standardised response mean), and prognostic calibration against 12-month mortality. An a priori acceptability threshold of ICC ≥0.70 between cAFI/48 and ALSFRS-R/48 will be used to define a "validated" index; if not achieved, the cAFI will be reported as a **functioning-utilisation composite** rather than an ALSFRS-R equivalent, and the Aim 2 analyses will be reframed accordingly.

**Trajectory modelling.**

- **Linear mixed-effects models** for the cAFI over time (time since index, in 90-day units), with random intercepts and random slopes, restricted cubic splines or piecewise-linear terms with a data-driven change point to capture accelerating late decline, and adjustment for age, sex, bulbar proxy, riluzole, NIV, PEG, and comorbidity. Between-group differences in slope (e.g., bulbar vs. limb onset; riluzole users vs. non-users) will be estimated as time × group interactions.
- **Latent-class growth mixture models (LCGMM)** to identify discrete progression phenotypes (e.g., slow, intermediate, rapidly progressive), with class number selected by BIC, entropy, and clinical interpretability; class membership will then be modelled with multinomial logistic regression against baseline predictors, and class-specific survival curves will be produced.
- **Joint modelling** of the longitudinal cAFI and time to death (shared random effects / joint latent class model) to obtain unbiased trajectory estimates in the presence of informative dropout, and to derive a dynamic individualised prediction of survival conditional on observed cAFI history. Dynamic prediction performance will be reported with time-dependent AUC and prediction error curves.
- **Informative missingness:** cAFI windows with no claims will be distinguished from true absence of utilisation by requiring continuous enrolment; missingness will be handled by the joint model's dropout sub-model rather than by imputation where markers are structurally absent.

### 7.3 Aim 3 — Survival and time to invasive ventilation

**Descriptive.** Kaplan–Meier curves for overall survival from index date and from symptom-onset proxy, overall and by sex, age group, onset-site proxy, riluzole use, and NIV initiation. Median survival with 95% CI (Brookmeyer–Crowley). Median follow-up by reverse Kaplan–Meier.

**Overall survival — Cox models.** Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models with age, sex, onset-site proxy, diagnostic delay, comorbidity index, care-setting and facility covariates, and riluzole as a **time-varying** exposure (current use with a 30-day grace period) to avoid immortal-time bias. A 6-month landmark analysis will be presented alongside the time-varying model. Proportional hazards will be tested with scaled Schoenfeld residuals and time-varying coefficients or restricted cubic splines for age/diagnostic delay if non-proportionality is detected. Facility-level clustering will be addressed with robust (sandwich) standard errors or shared frailty

**Title:** Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis in Taiwan: Incidence, Prevalence, Functional Decline, and Survival Using the National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD)

**Principal Investigator:** [Name]  
**Institution:** [Institution]  
**Version/Date:** 1.0, [Date]

---

### Abstract

Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a rapidly progressive neurodegenerative disease with median survival of 2–5 years. Taiwan’s National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD) offers a nationwide, population-based resource to study ALS epidemiology and outcomes. We propose a retrospective cohort study using NHIRD linked files Health-01 (outpatient), Health-02 (inpatient), Health-08 (catastrophic illness), and Health-10 (cause of death). Patients with ALS will be identified by ICD-10 G12.21 and catastrophic illness certification. Objectives are to (1) estimate annual incidence and prevalence, (2) model an ALSFRS-R-equivalent functional decline trajectory using healthcare utilization patterns, and (3) estimate overall survival and time to invasive ventilation, examining riluzole, non-invasive ventilation (NIV), and tracheostomy. We will use Poisson regression, Kaplan-Meier methods, Cox regression with time-varying covariates, competing-risk models, and mixed-effects models for longitudinal outcomes. Findings will inform national ALS care planning, reimbursement policy, and prognostication.

---

### 1. Background and Significance

ALS is a fatal motor neuron disease. Riluzole provides modest survival benefit, while NIV and tracheostomy can prolong survival and influence quality of life. Population-based data on ALS incidence, prevalence, functional decline, and ventilation timing in Taiwan are limited. The NHIRD covers nearly all Taiwanese residents and provides longitudinal claims data suitable for studying rare diseases. However, the NHIRD lacks direct clinical measures such as the ALS Functional Rating Scale–Revised (ALSFRS-R). We will therefore develop a claims-based ALSFRS-R-equivalent index (CAEI) using healthcare utilization trajectories as a surrogate for functional decline. This study will generate national estimates and identify factors associated with progression and survival.

---

### 2. Objectives

1. **Estimate incidence and prevalence** of ALS in Taiwan (2016–2023).
2. **Model ALSFRS-R-equivalent functional decline** using longitudinal healthcare utilization trajectories.
3. **Estimate overall survival and time to invasive ventilation**.
4. **Examine associations** with riluzole use, NIV, and tracheostomy, adjusting for demographic and clinical covariates.

---

### 3. Data Sources and Linkage Plan

We will apply to the National Health Research Institutes (NHRI) for the following NHIRD files:

- **Health-01:** Outpatient claims (diagnoses, procedures, medications, visits).
- **Health-02:** Inpatient claims (admissions, procedures, diagnoses, length of stay).
- **Health-08:** Catastrophic illness registry (ALS certification date, ICD code).
- **Health-10:** Cause of death registry (date and underlying cause of death).

**Linkage:** Deterministic linkage via scrambled patient ID, birth year, sex, and residence. Data will be analyzed in the NHRI secure environment. Study period: 2016-01-01 to 2023-12-31; follow-up through 2024-12-31. If extended to pre-2016, ICD-9-CM 335.20 will be used with validation against catastrophic illness registry.

---

### 4. Cohort Definition

**Source population:** All NHI beneficiaries.

**ALS case ascertainment:**
- At least one inpatient claim or two outpatient claims with ICD-10 G12.21 (or ICD-9-CM 335.20 for pre-2016), **and**
- Registration in Health-08 catastrophic illness registry for ALS.
- **Date of onset:** Earliest of first ALS diagnosis or catastrophic illness certification date.

**Incident cohort:** No ALS diagnosis in the prior 2 years (washout).  
**Prevalent cohort:** Alive with ALS diagnosis in a given calendar year.

**Inclusion criteria:**
- Continuous NHI enrollment.
- Age ≥20 years (all ages included; stratified analyses by age group).
- Available demographic data.

**Exclusion criteria:**
- Missing sex or birth year.
- Pre-existing ALS before 2016 (for incidence analyses).
- Death before cohort entry.

---

### 5. Exposure and Outcome Definitions

#### Exposures
- **Riluzole use:** ≥1 prescription (ATC N07XX02). Time-varying current use, cumulative duration, adherence (medication possession ratio ≥80%).
- **NIV:** NHI procedure/device codes for non-invasive ventilation and home respiratory care.
- **Tracheostomy:** NHI procedure codes for tracheostomy.
- **Invasive ventilation:** Endotracheal intubation or invasive mechanical ventilation.
- **Age at onset, sex.**

#### Outcomes
1. **Incidence and prevalence:** Annual incidence per 100,000 person-years; point prevalence per 100,000.
2. **Functional decline:** CAEI constructed from healthcare utilization: neurology visits, rehabilitation sessions, home care, emergency visits, hospital admissions, PEG/feeding tube, NIV, tracheostomy, wheelchair/mobility aids. Weights derived via factor analysis or item response theory; scaled to 0–48 (ALSFRS-R range). *Note: CAEI is a surrogate, not a direct ALSFRS-R measurement.*
3. **Overall survival:** Time from cohort entry to death (Health-10, all-cause). Cause-specific survival (ALS-related death: G12.21, respiratory failure J96.x) as secondary.
4. **Time to invasive ventilation:** Time to first tracheostomy or invasive mechanical ventilation. Secondary: time to NIV, time to any respiratory support, time to permanent ventilation.

#### Covariates
Age at onset, sex, Charlson Comorbidity Index, comorbidities (diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular, dementia, frontotemporal dementia, psychiatric, respiratory), socioeconomic status (income level, urbanization), hospital level, physician specialty, year of diagnosis, riluzole, NIV, tracheostomy.

---

### 6. Statistical Plan

#### 6.1 Incidence and Prevalence
- Annual incidence: Poisson regression; age-standardized to WHO 2000 population.
- Prevalence: log-binomial or Poisson regression with robust variance.
- Subgroup analyses by age, sex, and region.

#### 6.2 Functional Decline (CAEI)
- **Linear mixed-effects models:** CAEI_ij = β0 + β1 time + β2 time² + β3 riluzole + β4 NIV + β5 tracheostomy + covariates + b0i + b1i time + ε_ij. Random intercept and slope per patient. Time since onset as continuous with splines.
- **Generalized linear mixed models:** Negative binomial distribution for visit counts.
- **Latent class mixed models:** Identify fast vs. slow progressors.
- **Joint modeling:** Joint model of longitudinal CAEI and survival to account for informative dropout.
- **Validation:** If feasible, validate CAEI against ALSFRS-R in a hospital-based subset with separate IRB approval.

#### 6.3 Survival and Time to Invasive Ventilation
- **Kaplan-Meier** curves; log-rank tests. Median survival.
- **Cox proportional hazards regression** for overall survival. Time-varying covariates for riluzole, NIV, tracheostomy. Check proportional hazards assumption.
- **Competing risks:** Death as competing event for ventilation. Cumulative incidence function and Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards.
- **Immortal time bias:** Landmark analysis or time-dependent Cox models for riluzole/NIV/tracheostomy.
- **Propensity score:** Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) for riluzole to balance baseline covariates.
- **Subgroup analyses:** Age (<60 vs. ≥60), sex, riluzole use, NIV/tracheostomy, comorbidity burden.

#### 6.4 Sample Size and Power
Assuming ALS incidence of 1.5–2.0 per 100,000 and population ~23 million, we expect ~350–500 new cases/year, or ~3,000–4,000 incident cases over 2016–2023. With median survival ~3 years, this provides >80% power to detect hazard ratios of 1.25–1.30 for common exposures.

#### 6.5 Sensitivity Analyses
- Alternative washout periods (1 vs. 2 vs. 3 years).
- Exclude potential ALS mimics (e.g., cervical myelopathy, multifocal motor neuropathy).
- Multiple imputation for missing covariates.
- Negative control outcomes.
- Different CAEI weighting schemes.

### 8. Limitations

- Claims data lack direct clinical measures (ALSFRS-R, FVC, BMI, genetics).
- CAEI is a surrogate for functional decline and may misclassify.
- Coding errors and changes in ICD coding over time.
- Unmeasured confounding (e.g., lifestyle, socioeconomic factors).
- NIV/tracheostomy identification relies on procedure codes, which may be incomplete.

- Overall survival and time to invasive ventilation.
- Effect estimates for riluzole, NIV, and tracheostomy.
- Evidence to inform NHI reimbursement, palliative care planning, and respiratory support policies.

## NHRI Data-Application Research Proposal

**Title:** Disease Progression, Functional Decline, and Survival in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis: A Nationwide Population-Based Cohort Study Using the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD)

### 1. Background and Significance

Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a rapidly progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by loss of upper and lower motor neurons, leading to progressive bulbar, limb, and respiratory dysfunction. Median survival from diagnosis is typically 2–4 years, although clinical course is heterogeneous. In Taiwan, ALS is a catastrophic illness under the National Health Insurance (NHI) program, and incidence has been estimated at approximately 0.8–1.5 per 100,000 person-years, with prevalence around 4–7 per 100,000. However, nationwide, longitudinal evidence on disease progression, functional decline, and survival in Taiwan remains limited.

The NHIRD provides near-complete coverage of the Taiwanese population and includes outpatient claims, inpatient claims, catastrophic illness registration, and cause-of-death data. These data offer a unique opportunity to study ALS at the population level. However, the NHIRD does not contain direct clinical severity measures such as the Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Functional Rating Scale–Revised (ALSFRS-R). Therefore, a key methodological challenge is to derive a claims-based, ALSFRS-R-equivalent functional trajectory from healthcare utilization patterns. Such a measure could enable longitudinal modeling of functional decline and improve understanding of prognosis, treatment effects, and healthcare needs in ALS.

This study will estimate ALS incidence and prevalence, model functional decline using healthcare utilization trajectories, and estimate overall survival and time to invasive ventilation. Findings will inform clinical care, health policy, and future registry development in Taiwan.

### 2. Objectives

1. To estimate the incidence and prevalence of ALS in Taiwan, overall and by age, sex, calendar year, and geographic region.
2. To develop and validate a claims-based ALSFRS-R-equivalent functional score using healthcare utilization trajectories and to model longitudinal functional decline.
3. To estimate overall survival and time to invasive ventilation among patients with ALS, and to assess associations with riluzole use, non-invasive ventilation (NIV), tracheostomy, and other clinical and demographic factors.

### 3. Data Sources and Linkage

We request approval to use the following NHRI/HWDC databases:

| Database | Content | Use in this study |
|---|---|---|
| Health-01 | Outpatient claims | ALS diagnosis, visit dates, procedures, prescriptions, rehabilitation, NIV-related claims |
| Health-02 | Inpatient claims | ALS diagnosis, admissions, procedures, tracheostomy, invasive ventilation, ICU, length of stay |
| Health-08 | Catastrophic illness registry | ALS certification date, ICD code, definitive case ascertainment |
| Health-10 | Cause of death | Date of death, underlying and contributing causes of death |

Records will be linked by scrambled beneficiary identification number. The study period will span 2000–2020. ICD-9-CM code 335.20 will be used before 2016, and ICD-10-CM code G12.21 from 2016 onward.

### 4. Cohort Definition

**Source population:** All NHI beneficiaries in Taiwan during the study period.

**ALS case ascertainment:**
- **Definitive ALS:** Catastrophic illness registration for ALS in Health-08.
- **Probable ALS:** At least one inpatient claim with ICD-9-CM 335.20 or ICD-10-CM G12.21, OR at least two outpatient claims with the same code on different dates within 12 months.

**Incident cohort:**
- First ALS diagnosis after a 12-month washout period with no ALS code.
- Index date: earliest of first ALS claim or catastrophic illness registration date.
- Inclusion: age ≥18 years at index; continuous NHI enrollment for ≥12 months before index (unless ALS catastrophic illness certificate was issued at first contact).
- Exclusion: prior ALS diagnosis within 12 months; other motor neuron diseases (e.g., G12.0, G12.1) without ALS code; death before index; missing age or sex.

**Prevalent cohort:**
- All patients with an ALS diagnosis who were alive on December 31 of each calendar year.

**Follow-up:**
- From index date to death, disenrollment from NHI, or December 31, 2020, whichever occurred first.

### 5. Exposure and Outcomes

**Primary exposures of interest:**
- **Riluzole use:** Time-varying binary and cumulative exposure, defined by NHI drug codes (ATC N07XX02 or equivalent). Adherence will be estimated using proportion of days covered (PDC) or medication possession ratio (MPR).
- **NIV initiation:** Time-varying indicator for non-invasive ventilation, defined by procedure/device codes in outpatient or inpatient claims.
- **Tracheostomy/invasive ventilation:** Time-varying indicator for tracheostomy or invasive mechanical ventilation.

**Outcomes:**
1. **Incidence and prevalence** of ALS.
2. **Functional decline:** Claims-based ALSFRS-R-equivalent score (cALS-FS) derived from healthcare utilization.
3. **Overall survival:** Time from index date to all-cause death.
4. **Time to invasive ventilation:** Time from index date to first tracheostomy or invasive mechanical ventilation, with death as a competing risk.

**Covariates:**
- Age at onset (age at index date as proxy).
- Sex.
- Baseline comorbidities (Charlson or Elixhauser index) from the 12 months before index.
- Baseline healthcare utilization (outpatient visits, hospitalizations, ICU admissions).
- PEG placement, aspiration pneumonia, falls/fractures.
- Facility level and geographic region, if available.
- Calendar year.

### 6. Statistical Analysis Plan

#### 6.1 Incidence and Prevalence
- Annual incidence rate = number of incident ALS cases / person-years at risk in the NHI population.
- Age- and sex-standardized incidence rates will be calculated using the 2010 Taiwan population as the standard.
- Annual prevalence = number of living ALS cases on December 31 / mid-year population.
- Trends will be analyzed using Poisson or negative binomial regression and joinpoint regression to estimate annual percent change.
- Subgroup analyses will be performed by age group, sex, and region.

#### 6.2 Claims-Based ALSFRS-R-Equivalent Functional Decline
Because ALSFRS-R is not directly available, we will derive a claims-based functional score (cALS-FS) from healthcare utilization indicators mapped to ALSFRS-R domains:

- **Bulbar:** dysphagia diagnoses, PEG placement, speech therapy, aspiration pneumonia.
- **Upper limb:** occupational therapy, hand orthoses, assistive devices.
- **Lower limb:** physical therapy, walking aids, wheelchair use, falls/fractures.
- **Respiratory:** NIV, cough assist, oxygen therapy, respiratory failure, tracheostomy.

We will use item response theory (graded response model) or latent variable modeling to estimate a continuous functional score. If feasible, the score will be calibrated against ALSFRS-R in a validation subset from participating hospitals.

Longitudinal functional decline will be modeled using mixed-effects models:
\[
cALS\text{-}FS_{ij} = \beta_0 + b_{0i} + (\beta_1 + b_{1i})t_{ij} + \beta_2 \text{age} + \beta_3 \text{sex} + \beta_4 \text{riluzole}_{ij} + \beta_5 \text{NIV}_{ij} + \beta_6 \text{tracheostomy}_{ij} + \cdots + \varepsilon_{ij}
\]
where \(t_{ij}\) is time since index date, \(b_{0i}\) and \(b_{1i}\) are random intercept and slope, and time-varying exposures are updated at each visit. Restricted cubic splines will be used to capture nonlinear decline.

To address informative visit times and dropout due to death, we will use joint modeling of the longitudinal cALS-FS and the visit/survival process, with sensitivity analyses using inverse intensity weighting.

#### 6.3 Survival and Time to Invasive Ventilation
- **Overall survival:** Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank tests. Cox proportional hazards models will estimate hazard ratios for riluzole, NIV, tracheostomy, and covariates. Time-varying covariates will be used to avoid immortal time bias. Proportional hazards assumptions will be tested.
- **Time to invasive ventilation:** Competing risk analysis with death as a competing event. Cumulative incidence functions and Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models will be used, alongside cause-specific Cox models.
- **Landmark analyses:** At 3, 6, and 12 months to evaluate NIV and tracheostomy effects without immortal time bias.
- **Confounding control:** Propensity score matching or inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) will be used for riluzole, NIV, and tracheostomy, given confounding by indication.
- **Subgroup analyses:** Age (<60 vs ≥60), sex, riluzole use, NIV use, and calendar period.

#### 6.4 Sensitivity Analyses
- Vary ALS case definitions (definitive vs probable).
- Vary washout period (12 vs 24 months).
- Exclude ICD-9 period or analyze ICD-10 period separately.
- Exclude cases without catastrophic illness certification.
- E-value analysis for unmeasured confounding.
- Multiple imputation for missing covariates, if needed.

### 7. Feasibility and Sample Size

Taiwan has a population of approximately 23 million. With an ALS incidence of 0.8–1.5 per 100,000 person-years, we expect 200–350 new cases per year. Over 2010–2020, this yields an estimated 2,000–3,500 incident cases and a prevalent pool of 1,000–1,500 patients. These numbers are sufficient for survival analyses, longitudinal mixed models, and subgroup analyses. The NHIRD’s nationwide coverage and long follow-up minimize selection bias and loss to follow-up.

### 8. Ethical Considerations and Data Security

The study will be submitted for Institutional Review Board (IRB) approval. All data are de-identified and linked by scrambled identifiers. Analyses will be conducted on secure NHRI/HWDC servers. No individual-level data will be released. Results will be reported in aggregate form only.

### 9. Limitations

### 1. Background and Rationale

Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) is a rapidly progressive, fatal neurodegenerative disease characterized by the degeneration of upper and lower motor neurons. This leads to progressive muscle weakness, atrophy, and spasticity, ultimately resulting in respiratory failure and death, typically within 3-5 years of symptom onset. The global incidence is estimated at 1-2 per 100,000 person-years, but significant geographical and ethnic variations exist. In Taiwan, a comprehensive understanding of the ALS epidemiological landscape is still developing, with most data originating from single-center studies or registries that may not be fully representative of the national population.

The Taiwan National Health Insurance (NHI) system, a mandatory single-payer program covering over 99% of the population, provides an unparalleled resource for population-based research. The National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD) contains comprehensive longitudinal data on outpatient visits, hospitalizations, medications, and vital status. This database offers a unique opportunity to conduct a nationwide, long-term study of ALS.

Current knowledge gaps include:
1.  **Contemporary National Epidemiology:** Up-to-date and accurate estimates of ALS incidence and prevalence in Taiwan are lacking.
2.  **Disease Trajectory Modeling:** The progressive functional decline in ALS is clinically monitored using tools like the ALS Functional Rating Scale-Revised (ALSFRS-R). However, the NHIRD does not contain ALSFRS-R scores directly. A method to model functional decline using surrogate markers from healthcare utilization is needed.
3.  **Outcomes in the Real-World Setting:** While clinical trials provide data on survival and time to interventions like non-invasive ventilation (NIV) and tracheostomy, real-world data on these outcomes and their determinants (e.g., riluzole use) across the entire Taiwanese population are limited.

This study aims to address these gaps by leveraging the NHIRD to conduct a comprehensive analysis of ALS epidemiology, disease progression, and survival. The findings will inform clinical practice, healthcare resource allocation, and future research in Taiwan.

### 2. Research Objectives

1.  To estimate the annual incidence and period prevalence of ALS in Taiwan.
2.  To model ALS disease progression by constructing an ALSFRS-R-equivalent functional decline trajectory using healthcare utilization data.
3.  To estimate overall survival and time to key clinical milestones, specifically the initiation of non-invasive ventilation (NIV) and invasive ventilation (tracheostomy).
4.  To identify factors (demographics, riluzole use, interventions) associated with functional decline, survival, and time to ventilation.

### 3. Methods

#### 3.1. Data Sources and Linkage

This retrospective cohort study will utilize data from the NHIRD. The following datasets will be requested and linked using the scrambled, unique personal identifier:

- **Health-01 (Ambulatory Care):** Outpatient visit records, including diagnoses, visit dates, and prescribed medications (for riluzole).
- **Health-02 (Inpatient Care):** Hospitalization records, including admission/discharge dates, primary and secondary diagnoses, and procedures performed (e.g., tracheostomy).
- **Health-08 (Catastrophic Illness Registry):** This registry contains confirmed diagnoses for major diseases, including ALS. It serves as the primary source for identifying the ALS cohort due to its high diagnostic validity.
- **Health-10 (Cause of Death):** Vital status and underlying cause of death data.

#### 3.2. Cohort Definition

**Inclusion Criteria:**
- Patients with a first-ever diagnosis of ALS, identified by:
    - ICD-10-CM code **G12.21** (Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis) in the Catastrophic Illness Registry (Health-08).
    - The date of the first ALS-related outpatient visit or hospitalization will be defined as the **index date**.
- To ensure incident cases, we will apply a **washout period** of at least one year prior to the index date, during which no ALS diagnosis (ICD-10 G12.21 or ICD-9 335.20) is recorded.
- Patients must have at least one year of continuous NHI enrollment prior to their index date to ensure complete baseline data.

**Exclusion Criteria:**
- Patients with other forms of motor neuron disease (e.g., progressive muscular atrophy, primary lateral sclerosis) or other conditions that can mimic ALS.
- Patients diagnosed with ALS before the start of the study period.

#### 3.3. Exposure and Covariates

- **Primary Exposure:** **Riluzole use**, defined as a prescription for riluzole (Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical [ATC] code N07XX02) filled at any point after the index date. It will be analyzed as a time-varying covariate (current/former/never use).
- **Key Covariates:**
    - **Age at Onset:** Age at the index date.
    - **Sex:** Male or Female.
    - **NIV/Tracheostomy:** Identified via procedure codes in inpatient and outpatient records. These will be treated as time-varying covariates and as study outcomes.
    - **Baseline Comorbidities:** Elixhauser Comorbidity Index score calculated from diagnoses in the year prior to the index date.
    - **Healthcare Utilization:** Baseline number of outpatient visits and hospitalizations in the year prior to the index date.

#### 3.4. Outcome Definitions

1.  **Incidence and Prevalence:**
    - **Incidence:** Number of new ALS cases (per our incident cohort definition) divided by the total person-years at risk in the Taiwanese population for each calendar year. Denominators will be obtained from the Ministry of the Interior's population statistics.
    - **Prevalence:** Total number of living ALS patients (from our cohort) on December 31st of each year, divided by the total mid-year population.

2.  **Functional Decline (ALSFRS-R Equivalent):**
    - We will construct a proxy measure for functional decline using a composite score derived from healthcare utilization data, inspired by validated approaches. The score will be calculated for each 3-month interval following the index date and will incorporate:
        - **Hospitalizations:** Number and duration of ALS-related hospitalizations.
        - **Outpatient Visits:** Number of ALS-related outpatient visits, particularly to neurology and pulmonology.
        - **New Interventions/Comorbidities:** Occurrence of new diagnoses indicating disease progression (e.g., pneumonia, respiratory failure, dysphagia, falls).
        - **Medication Changes:** Introduction of new symptomatic medications (e.g., for spasticity, secretions).
    - A weighted score will be developed, with higher scores indicating greater functional impairment and disease progression. The trajectory of this score over time will be the primary outcome for Objective 2.

3.  **Survival and Time-to-Event Outcomes:**
    - **Overall Survival:** Time from the index date to death from any cause (from Health-10).
    - **Time to Invasive Ventilation:** Time from the index date to the first tracheostomy procedure.
    - **Time to NIV:** Time from the index date to the first NIV initiation. Censoring will occur at death, end of study period (Dec 31, 2020), or loss to follow-up (dismantlement from NHI).

### 4. Statistical Plan

#### 4.1. Descriptive Analysis
Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics will be summarized using means and standard deviations or medians and interquartile ranges for continuous variables, and counts and percentages for categorical variables. Incidence and prevalence rates will be presented with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), stratified by age and sex.

#### 4.2. Modeling Functional Decline
To model the ALSFRS-R-equivalent functional decline trajectory, we will use **mixed-effects models (linear or non-linear)** .
- The proxy functional decline score will be the dependent variable.
- Time (in 3-month intervals from the index date) will be the primary independent variable.
- A random intercept and random slope for time will be included for each patient to account for individual variability in baseline function and rate of decline.
- Fixed effects will include age at onset, sex, riluzole use (time-varying), and baseline comorbidities. This will allow us to estimate the average trajectory and identify factors that modify the rate of decline.

#### 4.3. Survival Analysis
- **Kaplan-Meier Method:** We will generate Kaplan-Meier survival curves for overall survival and time to ventilation (NIV and tracheostomy). The log-rank test will be used to compare survival distributions across different subgroups (e.g., by riluzole use, age group, sex).
- **Cox Proportional Hazards Regression:** To estimate the effect of covariates on the risk of death and time to ventilation, we will build multivariable Cox proportional hazards models.
    - The model will be adjusted for age at onset, sex, riluzole use (as a time-varying covariate), baseline comorbidity score, and other clinically relevant covariates.
    - The proportional hazards assumption will be tested using Schoenfeld residuals.
    - Hazard ratios (HRs) and their 95% CIs will be reported.

### 5. Ethical Considerations

This study involves the analysis of de-identified secondary data from the NHIRD. The protocol will be submitted for review and approval by the Institutional Review Board (IRB) of our institution and the NHRI Data Release Review Committee. All data will be handled in accordance with NHRI data security and privacy regulations.

### 6. Expected Outcomes and Significance

This study is expected to produce several significant outcomes:
1.  **Robust Epidemiological Data:** It will provide the most current and comprehensive estimates of ALS incidence and prevalence in Taiwan, stratified by key demographic factors. This is crucial for public health planning and resource allocation.
2.  **Novel Disease Progression Model:** The development of a validated, data-driven proxy for functional decline will be a methodological innovation, enabling the study of ALS progression in large administrative databases where clinical scores are unavailable.
3.  **Real-World Evidence on Interventions:** The study will provide real-world evidence on the effectiveness of riluzole and the timing of respiratory support (NIV/tracheostomy) in a national cohort, complementing findings from clinical trials.
4.  **Identification of Prognostic Factors:** By linking patient characteristics and treatment patterns to outcomes, we will identify factors associated with faster progression and poorer survival, which can help guide clinical management and patient counseling.

Ultimately, this research will significantly enhance our understanding of ALS in Taiwan and provide an evidence base to improve patient care and outcomes.

### 7. Limitations

- **Lack of Clinical Detail:** The primary limitation is the absence of direct clinical data, such as ALSFRS-R scores, genetic information, and precise dates of symptom onset. Our proxy for functional decline, while innovative, is an indirect measure.
- **Diagnostic Validity:** The accuracy of ALS diagnosis relies on the Catastrophic Illness Registry. While this registry has high validity, misclassification is possible.
- **Confounding by Indication:** Patients prescribed riluzole may differ systematically from those who are not, potentially leading to confounding by indication, which we will attempt to mitigate with multivariable adjustment.
- **Data Censoring:** Loss to follow-up due to individuals leaving the NHI system or the study period ending will be handled via censoring in survival analyses, but could introduce bias if it is non-random.

## 2. Cost-effective application strategy

**Governing cost principles (from the supplied rules):**

1. **Per-field-per-year billing.** Every standard file is charged by selected field × selected year. Adding one year across a ten-field request multiplies the cost tenfold; adding one field across ten years multiplies it tenfold.
2. **Separate applications, sequenced by evidence.** Phase 1 is submitted as the smallest standalone application; Phase 2 and Phase 3 are only submitted after their decision gates are passed. This prevents paying for Phase 3 years before Phase 1 has shown that the cohort and event dates are stable.
3. **Duplicate fields are not free.** Fields requested in more than one of Health-01/Health-02/Health-03 (for example `ID`, `HOSP_ID`, `FEE_YM`, `APPL_DATE`, `FUNC_TYPE`, `PAY_TYPE`, diagnosis codes) are counted separately for each dataset in which they are selected. Assume duplicate or near-duplicate fields are counted per dataset-per-year and verify the counting rule in the official NHRI application system.
4. **Over-half-field briefing threshold.** Rules note a briefing/justification threshold for Health-01/Health-02/Health-03 when the requested fields exceed half of a file's total field count. The exact trigger, the denominator, and the required format must be confirmed in the official NHRI application system before submission; Phase 3 is the phase most likely to cross it.
5. **Year-less ("不分年度") datasets.** Health-08 and Health-51 are listed as 不分年度 in all three phases, so year selection does not apply to them. Confirm in the official system whether their charge is field-based without a year multiplier; do not assume.
6. **Medical-type selector (醫別).** Health-01 is requested with 醫別 = 西醫 in all three phases; Health-04 is requested with 醫別 = 西醫 in Phase 3. The selector is available for 西醫, 中醫, 牙醫 — restricting to 西醫 is the minimum-necessary choice and must be shown as such.
7. **Full-date fields are an explicit special request.** Health-01 `FUNC_DATE` (field 12) and Health-02 `IN_DATE` (field 13) are needed as complete dates (含年月日). This obliges the applicant to mark page 8 "特殊需求申請(選填)" as **是** and to state **需使用完整日期欄位（含年月日）**, with the specific fields checked and individually justified. In Phase 3 the same logic extends to the Health-03 full-date field (`FUNC_DATE`, field 14) — confirm whether it must also be listed on page 8.
8. **Pharmacy/order files are the most expensive lever.** Health-03/04/05/07 are added only in Phase 3 and are the dominant cost driver. Their inclusion must be defended by a treatment or cost question that actually changes a decision (riluzole persistence, ventilation/tracheostomy procedures, resource consumption), not by general completeness.

**Title:** Disease Progression, Functional Decline, and Survival in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis: A Population-Based Study Using the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD)

---

### 1. Background

Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a rapidly progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by loss of upper and lower motor neurons, leading to progressive bulbar, limb, and respiratory dysfunction. Median survival from symptom onset is approximately 2–5 years, with respiratory failure as the leading cause of death. In Taiwan, ALS is recognized as a catastrophic illness, and patients are eligible for expedited NHI reimbursement and multidisciplinary care. However, population-level data on ALS incidence, prevalence, real-world disease trajectories, and survival remain limited.

The Taiwan NHIRD covers >99% of the population and provides longitudinal claims data on outpatient visits, inpatient care, catastrophic illness registration, and cause of death. These data offer a unique opportunity to study ALS at a national scale. Because the NHIRD does not contain the ALS Functional Rating Scale–Revised (ALSFRS-R), we propose to derive a claims-based ALSFRS-R-equivalent functional decline proxy using healthcare utilization trajectories. This study will quantify the burden of ALS in Taiwan, model functional decline, and identify factors associated with overall survival and time to invasive ventilation.

**Objectives:**
1. Estimate the incidence and prevalence of ALS (ICD-10 G12.21) in Taiwan from 2016 to 2023.
2. Model ALSFRS-R-equivalent functional decline using healthcare utilization trajectories.
3. Estimate overall survival and time to invasive ventilation, and evaluate associations with age at onset, sex, riluzole use, and NIV/tracheostomy.

---

### 2. Data Sources and Linkage

We request approval to access and link the following NHRI datasets using encrypted beneficiary IDs:

- **Health-01:** Outpatient claims (visit dates, diagnoses, specialty, procedures, prescriptions).
- **Health-02:** Inpatient claims (admission/discharge dates, diagnoses, procedures, ICU care, mechanical ventilation).
- **Health-08:** Catastrophic illness registry (ALS certification, registration date, ICD-10 G12.21).
- **Health-10:** Cause of death data (date and underlying cause of death).

Linkage will be performed by the NHRI using consistent scrambled patient identifiers. All analyses will be conducted in the secure HWDC/NHRI environment. The study will be approved by the relevant Institutional Review Board (IRB) and the NHRI Data Release Review Committee.

**Study period:** January 1, 2016 – December 31, 2023.  
**Washout period:** January 1, 2014 – December 31, 2015, using ICD-9 335.20 and ICD-10 G12.21 to identify pre-existing ALS.

---

### 3. Cohort Definition

**Inclusion criteria:**
- At least one of the following:
  - One inpatient diagnosis of ICD-10 G12.21 (amyotrophic lateral sclerosis), or
  - Two outpatient diagnoses of ICD-10 G12.21 within 12 months, or
  - Catastrophic illness registration for ALS in Health-08.
- Age ≥20 years at index date.

**Index date:** Earliest date of ALS diagnosis (inpatient or outpatient) or catastrophic illness registration, whichever comes first.

**Incident cohort:** Patients with first ALS diagnosis between January 1, 2017 and December 31, 2023, with no prior ALS diagnosis (ICD-9 335.20 or ICD-10 G12.21) during the washout period.

**Prevalent cohort:** All patients with ALS who were alive on December 31 of each calendar year (2016–2023).

**Exclusions:**
- Age <20 years at index.
- Missing sex or birth date.
- Death date before index date.
- Other motor neuron diseases (e.g., G12.0–G12.2 excluding G12.21) if clinically inconsistent with ALS; sensitivity analyses will include/exclude these cases.

**Follow-up:** From index date to death, disenrollment, or December 31, 2023, whichever occurs first.

---

### 4. Exposure and Covariates

**Primary exposures/covariates:**
- **Age at onset:** Proxy using age at index date.
- **Sex:** From enrollment data.
- **Riluzole use:** Time-varying exposure from outpatient pharmacy claims (ATC code N07XX02). Defined as current use (prescription within 30 days), cumulative defined daily dose (cDDD), and proportion of days covered (PDC).
- **Non-invasive ventilation (NIV):** Time-varying exposure using NHI procedure codes for non-invasive positive pressure ventilation.
- **Tracheostomy/invasive ventilation:** Time-varying exposure using NHI procedure codes or ICD-10-PCS codes for tracheostomy and invasive mechanical ventilation.

**Additional covariates:**
- Urbanization level and geographic region (from NHIRD enrollment).
- Baseline comorbidities: Charlson Comorbidity Index, Elixhauser score, hypertension, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, COPD, dementia, depression.
- Baseline ALS-related interventions: PEG insertion, wheelchair/assistive device prescriptions, respiratory infections.
- If available, edaravone use (ATC code N07XXxx) as a time-varying covariate.

---

### 5. Outcomes

**5.1 Incidence and prevalence**
- Annual incidence rate per 100,000 person-years, age- and sex-standardized to the WHO 2000 population.
- Annual point prevalence per 100,000 population on December 31.
- Trends over time using Poisson regression.

**5.2 ALSFRS-R-equivalent functional decline proxy**
Because ALSFRS-R is not available in claims data, we will construct a **Claims-Based ALS Functional Decline Proxy (cAFDP)** from monthly healthcare utilization. Domains will mirror ALSFRS-R:
- **Bulbar:** PEG insertion, speech therapy, aspiration pneumonia, dysphagia-related visits.
- **Fine motor:** Occupational therapy, assistive device prescriptions, home modifications.
- **Gross motor:** Wheelchair/walker prescriptions, physical therapy, falls/fractures.
- **Respiratory:** NIV initiation, cough assist, oxygen therapy, respiratory infections, respiratory failure, tracheostomy.

Each domain will be scored monthly based on utilization events. Domain scores will be combined using factor analysis or item response theory to generate a continuous cAFDP score (0–48 scale analog). The cAFDP will be validated internally against mortality, time to ventilation, and catastrophic illness registration.

**5.3 Survival outcomes**
- **Overall survival:** All-cause mortality from Health-10.
- **Time to invasive ventilation:** First date of tracheostomy or invasive mechanical ventilation (excluding perioperative ventilation <24 hours).

---

### 6. Statistical Plan

**6.1 Descriptive analysis**
Baseline characteristics will be summarized by sex, age group, riluzole use, and NIV/tracheostomy status. Continuous variables will be presented as mean ± SD or median (IQR); categorical variables as counts and percentages.

**6.2 Incidence and prevalence**
Incidence rates and prevalence will be calculated with 95% confidence intervals using Poisson exact methods. Age-sex standardized rates will be computed. Joinpoint regression will assess temporal trends.

**6.3 Functional decline modeling**
Linear mixed-effects models will be used to model cAFDP trajectories:
\[
Y_{ij} = (\beta_0 + b_{0i}) + (\beta_1 + b_{1i})t_{ij} + \beta_2 t_{ij}^2 + \beta_3 X_i + \beta_4 Z_{ij} + \epsilon_{ij}
\]
where \(Y_{ij}\) is the cAFDP score for patient \(i\) at month \(j\), \(t_{ij}\) is time since index, \(b_{0i}\) and \(b_{1i}\) are random intercept and slope, \(X_i\) are baseline covariates, and \(Z_{ij}\) are time-varying covariates (riluzole, NIV, tracheostomy). Splines or piecewise linear terms will be used to capture non-linear decline. Domain-specific models will also be fitted. Sensitivity analyses will use joint modeling of longitudinal cAFDP and survival to account for informative dropout.

**6.4 Survival analysis**
- **Kaplan-Meier** curves will estimate overall survival and time to invasive ventilation, with log-rank tests for group comparisons.
- **Cox proportional hazards models** will estimate hazard ratios (HRs) for age, sex, riluzole use, NIV, tracheostomy, and cAFDP. Riluzole, NIV, and tracheostomy will be modeled as time-varying covariates to avoid immortal time bias.
- **Competing risk analysis:** For time to invasive ventilation, death is a competing event. Cumulative incidence functions and Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards will be used, alongside cause-specific Cox models.
- **Proportional hazards assumption** will be checked using Schoenfeld residuals and time-dependent covariates if needed.
- **Landmark analysis** at 6 and 12 months will assess whether early cAFDP decline predicts subsequent mortality.

**6.5 Sample size and power**
Based on an estimated ALS incidence of 1.5–2.0 per 100,000 person-years in Taiwan, we expect approximately 300–450 incident cases per year and 2,500–3,500 cases over 2016–2023. With this sample size, we will have >80% power to detect a hazard ratio of 1.3 for common exposures (e.g., riluzole, NIV) at a two-sided α = 0.05.

**6.6 Sensitivity analyses**
- Alternative cohort definitions (catastrophic illness only vs. claims-based).
- Exclusion of prevalent cases with different washout periods.
- Restriction to patients with ≥2 outpatient ALS diagnoses.
- Validation of cAFDP against external clinical ALS registry data, if linkage is feasible.
- Multiple imputation for missing covariates.

---

### 7. Ethical Considerations and Data Management

This study will use de-identified administrative data. All analyses will be performed in the NHRI/HWDC secure environment. No attempts will be made to re-identify individuals. The study protocol will be submitted for IRB approval and NHRI data access review. Results will be reported in aggregate form only.

---

### 8. Expected Contributions

This study will provide the first nationwide estimates of ALS incidence, prevalence, and real-world disease progression in Taiwan. The cAFDP will offer a scalable method to model functional decline using claims data, enabling comparative effectiveness research on riluzole, NIV, and tracheostomy. Findings will inform clinical guidelines, health policy, and resource allocation for ALS care in Taiwan and other Asian populations.

Use three separate, gated applications rather than one large application. This matches the skeleton’s phased logic and minimizes review risk and cost.

# NHRI Data-Application Research Proposal

## Title
**Disease Progression, Functional Decline, and Survival in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis: A Population-Based Cohort Study Using the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD)**

## 1. Background and Significance
Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a progressive, fatal neurodegenerative disease characterised by loss of upper and lower motor neurons. Median survival from symptom onset is typically 2–5 years, although the clinical course is highly heterogeneous. Riluzole provides a modest survival benefit, while non-invasive ventilation (NIV) and tracheostomy with invasive ventilation can prolong survival but substantially alter quality of life and care needs. Population-based estimates of ALS incidence, prevalence, functional decline, and survival are essential for healthcare planning, resource allocation, and evaluation of real-world treatment patterns.

Taiwan’s National Health Insurance (NHI) system covers more than 99% of the population and has accumulated longitudinal claims data since 1997. The National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD), managed by the National Health Research Institutes (NHRI), provides an ideal platform for studying rare diseases such as ALS. The catastrophic illness registry (Health-08) further allows confirmation of ALS diagnoses and captures patients eligible for copayment waiver. However, contemporary population-based data on ALS in Taiwan remain limited, particularly regarding functional decline proxies, survival, and time to invasive ventilation.

This study will use linked NHIRD datasets to:
1. Estimate the incidence and prevalence of ALS in Taiwan.
2. Develop and model an ALSFRS-R-equivalent functional decline trajectory using healthcare utilisation patterns.
3. Estimate overall survival and time to invasive ventilation, and identify associated factors including riluzole use, NIV, and tracheostomy.

## 2. Objectives
**Primary objectives**
1. To estimate annual incidence and prevalence of ALS (ICD-10 G12.21) in Taiwan, overall and by age and sex.
2. To model longitudinal functional decline using a claims-based ALSFRS-R-equivalent index derived from healthcare utilisation trajectories.
3. To estimate overall survival and time to invasive ventilation from ALS diagnosis, and to evaluate predictors including age at onset, sex, riluzole use, NIV, and tracheostomy.

**Secondary objectives**
- To describe real-world patterns of riluzole use, NIV, and tracheostomy.
- To identify subgroups with rapid functional decline or poor survival.
- To assess the association between healthcare utilisation trajectories and clinical outcomes.

| Dataset | Content | Use in this study |
|---|---|---|
| **Health-01** | Outpatient care claims | ALS diagnosis, outpatient visits, procedures, drug prescriptions, rehabilitation, NIV/oxygen codes |

**Study period:** 2000–2023, or the latest year available at the time of data release. Because Taiwan transitioned from ICD-9-CM to ICD-10-CM/PCS in 2016, ALS will be identified using:
- ICD-9-CM **335.20** for claims before 2016.
- ICD-10-CM **G12.21** for claims from 2016 onward.

A sensitivity analysis will be restricted to 2016–2023 to assess the impact of coding transition.

## 4. Cohort Definition
### 4.1 Source population
All beneficiaries in the NHIRD during the study period.

### 4.2 Inclusion criteria
Patients will be included if they meet at least one of the following:
1. At least one outpatient or inpatient claim with a diagnosis of ALS (ICD-10 G12.21 or ICD-9 335.20).
2. A catastrophic illness certificate for ALS recorded in Health-08.

### 4.3 Confirmed ALS cohort
To improve diagnostic validity, ALS will be considered confirmed if at least one of the following is present:
- Catastrophic illness certification for ALS; or
- ≥2 outpatient visits with ALS diagnosis on different dates within 12 months; or
- ≥1 inpatient admission with ALS as a primary or secondary diagnosis.

### 4.4 Incident and prevalent cohorts
- **Incident cohort:** First ALS diagnosis or catastrophic illness certification during the study period, with no prior ALS diagnosis or certification in a 2-year washout period. The **index date** is the earliest date of ALS diagnosis or certification.
- **Prevalent cohort:** Any patient with a confirmed ALS diagnosis or certification who is alive on December 31 of each calendar year.

### 4.5 Exclusion criteria
- Age <20 years at index date (or <18 years, depending on NHRI data policy).
- Missing sex or birth date.
- Prevalent ALS cases at the start of the incidence washout period.
- Diagnoses of other motor neuron diseases if ALS is not confirmed.

### 4.6 Follow-up
Patients will be followed from the index date until:
- Death (Health-10),
- End of study period,
- Disenrollment from NHI, or
- For functional decline analyses, quarterly intervals until death or end of follow-up.

## 5. Exposure and Outcome Definitions
### 5.1 Exposures and covariates
- **Age at onset:** Age at index date.
- **Sex:** Male/female.
- **Riluzole use:** Prescription of riluzole (ATC N07XX02 or pre-specified NHI drug codes). Definitions will include ever/never use, current use, cumulative duration, and adherence (proportion of days covered or medication possession ratio).
- **NIV:** Non-invasive ventilation identified by NHI procedure/equipment codes in outpatient or inpatient claims.
- **Tracheostomy/invasive ventilation:** Tracheostomy or invasive mechanical ventilation identified by NHI procedure codes in inpatient claims.
- **Other covariates:** PEG insertion, rehabilitation, assistive devices, comorbidities (Charlson or Elixhauser index), hospitalisations, emergency visits, ICU admissions, and urbanisation level if available.

### 5.2 Outcomes
**Objective 1: Incidence and prevalence**
- Annual incidence rate per 100,000 person-years.
- Annual point prevalence (alive on December 31) and period prevalence (any ALS diagnosis during the year) per 100,000 beneficiaries.

**Objective 2: ALSFRS-R-equivalent functional decline**
Because NHIRD does not contain the ALS Functional Rating Scale-Revised (ALSFRS-R), we will derive a claims-based ALSFRS-R-equivalent index (cALSFRS-R) from healthcare utilisation trajectories. The index will be developed using a pre-specified mapping of claims-based indicators to functional domains:

| Domain | Candidate claims-based indicators |
|---|---|
| Bulbar | PEG insertion, speech therapy, aspiration pneumonia admissions |
| Fine motor | Occupational therapy, assistive device codes |
| Gross motor | Wheelchair, physical therapy, gait aids, falls |
| Respiratory | NIV, oxygen, respiratory therapy, respiratory failure admissions |
| General | Emergency visits, hospitalisations, ICU admissions |

Using item response theory (IRT) or confirmatory factor analysis, we will model the probability of observing each indicator as a function of an underlying latent functional severity score. The latent score will be linearly transformed to a 0–48 scale, with higher scores indicating better function. The cALSFRS-R will be computed quarterly for each patient. Internal validation will include correlation with time to death, time to invasive ventilation, and hospitalisation.

**Objective 3: Overall survival and time to invasive ventilation**
- **Overall survival:** Time from index date to death from any cause (Health-10) or censoring at end of follow-up.
- **Time to invasive ventilation:** Time from index date to first tracheostomy or invasive mechanical ventilation, censored at death or end of follow-up. Death will be treated as a competing risk.

## 6. Statistical Analysis Plan
### 6.1 Descriptive analyses
Baseline characteristics will be summarised by age, sex, riluzole use, NIV, tracheostomy, comorbidities, and year of diagnosis. Continuous variables will be reported as mean ± SD or median (IQR); categorical variables as counts and percentages.

### 6.2 Incidence and prevalence
- Annual incidence rates will be calculated as the number of new ALS cases divided by person-years at risk, expressed per 100,000 person-years with 95% confidence intervals (Poisson exact).
- Prevalence will be calculated as the number of prevalent cases divided by the total NHI beneficiary population on December 31 (point prevalence) or during the year (period prevalence).
- Rates will be age- and sex-standardised to the Taiwan 2000 population or WHO standard population.
- Trends over time will be assessed using Poisson or negative binomial regression.

### 6.3 Survival analyses
- Kaplan-Meier curves will estimate overall survival and time to invasive ventilation. Median survival with 95% CI will be reported.
- Cox proportional hazards models will estimate hazard ratios for overall survival and time to invasive ventilation. Covariates will include age at onset (continuous, restricted cubic splines), sex, riluzole use (time-dependent), NIV (time-dependent), tracheostomy (time-dependent), PEG, comorbidities, and year of diagnosis.
- Proportional hazards assumptions will be checked using Schoenfeld residuals. If violated, time-varying coefficients or stratified Cox models will be used.
- To avoid immortal time bias, riluzole, NIV, and tracheostomy will be modelled as time-dependent covariates. Landmark analyses at 3, 6, and 12 months will be performed as sensitivity analyses.
- For time to invasive ventilation, death will be treated as a competing risk. Cumulative incidence functions and Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models will be used, alongside cause-specific Cox models.

### 6.4 Longitudinal functional decline
- Linear mixed-effects models will be used to model cALSFRS-R trajectories over time:
  \[
  \text{cALSFRS-R}_{ij} = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{time}_{ij} + \beta_2 \text{age} + \beta_3 \text{sex} + \beta_4 \text{riluzole} + \beta_5 \text{NIV} + \beta_6 \text{tracheostomy} + \ldots + b_{0i} + b_{1i}\text{time}_{ij} + \varepsilon_{ij}
  \]
  where \(b_{0i}\) and \(b_{1i}\) are random intercept and slope. Time will be modelled as years since index, with restricted cubic splines or piecewise linear terms to capture non-linear decline.
- Annual rate of decline will be estimated overall and by subgroup (age, sex, riluzole use, NIV, tracheostomy).
- Healthcare utilisation trajectories (e.g., counts of outpatient visits, rehabilitation sessions, emergency visits, hospitalisations) will be modelled using generalised linear mixed models (Poisson or negative binomial) with random intercepts.
- Latent class mixed models or group-based trajectory models will identify distinct functional decline phenotypes. These phenotypes will be associated with survival and time to invasive ventilation.
- To account for informative dropout due to death, joint modelling of longitudinal cALSFRS-R and survival will be performed as a sensitivity analysis.

### 6.5 Missing data and sensitivity analyses
- Multiple imputation will be used for missing covariates if applicable.
- Sensitivity analyses will include:
  - Alternative ALS definitions (catastrophic illness only vs. claims-based).
  - ICD-9 vs. ICD-10 periods.
  - Exclusion of patients with a single outpatient diagnosis.
  - Varying washout periods (1, 2, and 5 years).
  - Complete-case analysis vs. imputed analysis.
  - Restriction to patients with ≥1 year of follow-up.

### 6.6 Software
Analyses will be performed using SAS 9.4, R 4.3 or later, and Stata 17 or later.

## 7. Ethical Considerations and Data Security
- The study will be submitted for approval by the Institutional Review Board (IRB) of the participating institution.
- All NHIRD data are de-identified and encrypted by NHRI. No personal identifiers will be accessible.
- Data will be stored and analysed on a secure, password-protected server compliant with NHRI data governance requirements.
- Only aggregate results will be reported; no individual-level data will be published.
- The study will comply with the Taiwan Personal Data Protection Act and NHRI data application regulations.

## 8. Limitations
- NHIRD lacks clinical measures such as ALSFRS-R, forced vital capacity, genetic testing, and precise symptom onset date.
- The cALSFRS-R is a claims-based proxy and may not perfectly reflect clinical functional status.
- Coding errors and underreporting of procedures (e.g., NIV, tracheostomy) may occur.
- Cause of death data may have inaccuracies.
- Unmeasured confounders (e.g., socioeconomic status, caregiver support, clinical care setting) may influence outcomes.
- The transition from ICD-9 to ICD-10 may introduce coding artifacts.

## 9. Expected Contributions
This study will provide contemporary, population-based estimates of ALS incidence, prevalence, functional decline, and survival in Taiwan. It will generate real-world evidence on the use and effectiveness of riluzole, NIV, and tracheostomy, and identify subgroups at high risk of rapid progression. The findings will inform clinical practice, healthcare resource allocation, and future ALS research in Taiwan and other Asian populations.

**Title:** Disease Progression, Functional Decline, and Survival in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis: A Nationwide Population-Based Study Using the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD)

---

## 1. Background and Rationale

Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a rapidly progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by loss of upper and lower motor neurons, leading to progressive functional decline, respiratory failure, and death, with median survival typically 2–5 years from symptom onset. In Taiwan, ALS is recognized as a catastrophic illness, and patients are eligible for a catastrophic illness certificate. The Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD) covers >99% of the population and provides longitudinal claims data on outpatient visits, hospitalizations, procedures, medications, and catastrophic illness registration, making it an ideal resource for nationwide epidemiological and outcomes research.

However, previous studies on ALS in Taiwan have often been limited by small sample sizes, single-center designs, short follow-up, or lack of longitudinal functional trajectories. Direct measures of functional status, such as the ALS Functional Rating Scale-Revised (ALSFRS-R), are not available in claims data. Therefore, there is a need to develop a claims-based proxy for ALS functional decline using healthcare utilization trajectories. Such a tool would allow nationwide estimation of disease progression, survival, and time to invasive ventilation, and would inform clinical practice and health policy.

This proposal aims to establish a nationwide ALS cohort using the NHIRD, estimate incidence and prevalence, model an ALSFRS-R-equivalent functional decline score from healthcare utilization, and estimate overall survival and time to invasive ventilation. We will also evaluate the impact of riluzole use, non-invasive ventilation (NIV), and tracheostomy on outcomes.

---

## 2. Study Aims

**Aim 1:** Estimate the annual incidence and prevalence of ALS (ICD-10 G12.21) in Taiwan from 2016 to 2020, overall and by age, sex, and urbanization level.

**Aim 2:** Develop and model a claims-based ALSFRS-R-equivalent functional decline score (cALSFRS-R) using longitudinal healthcare utilization trajectories.

**Aim 3:** Estimate overall survival and time to invasive ventilation, and identify predictors including age at onset, sex, riluzole use, NIV, and tracheostomy.

---

## 3. Methods

### 3.1 Data Sources and Linkage

We will request the following NHIRD datasets through the NHRI data application process:

- **Health-01 (Outpatient Claims):** diagnoses, visit dates, procedures, medications.
- **Health-02 (Inpatient Claims):** admissions, diagnoses, procedures, ICU care, mechanical ventilation.
- **Health-08 (Catastrophic Illness Registry):** ALS certification, diagnosis date, ICD-10 code.
- **Health-10 (Cause of Death):** date and cause of death.
- **Registry for Beneficiaries (if available):** for denominator and enrollment status.

All datasets will be linked by encrypted beneficiary ID. The study period will be 2016–2020, with a 2-year washout period (2014–2015) using both ICD-9-CM 335.20 and ICD-10-CM G12.21 to identify pre-existing cases. If data availability permits, the study period will be extended to 2021.

### 3.2 Cohort Definition

**Source population:** All National Health Insurance beneficiaries in Taiwan.

**Inclusion criteria (confirmed ALS):**
- At least one Health-08 catastrophic illness certificate for ALS (ICD-10 G12.21), **or**
- At least two outpatient diagnoses of G12.21 separated by ≥30 days, **or**
- At least one inpatient diagnosis of G12.21.

**Index date:** The earliest date of ALS diagnosis or catastrophic illness registration, whichever occurs first.

**Exclusion criteria:**
- Age <20 years at index date.
- Pre-existing ALS diagnosis before the washout period.
- Other motor neuron diseases (e.g., G12.20, G12.22, G12.29) or ALS mimic diagnoses (e.g., spinal muscular atrophy, primary lateral sclerosis).
- Missing age or sex.
- Death before index date.

**Follow-up:** From index date to death, end of study period (2020-12-31), or NHI deregistration, whichever occurs first.

### 3.3 Exposure and Outcomes

**Exposures:**
- **Riluzole use:** Identified from outpatient pharmacy claims using ATC code N07XX02 or NHI drug codes. Treated as a time-varying exposure (current use vs. never/former).
- **NIV:** Identified from inpatient/outpatient procedure or device codes.
- **Tracheostomy:** Identified from inpatient procedure codes (ICD-10-PCS or NHI procedure codes).
- **Age at onset:** Age at index date.
- **Sex:** Male/female.

**Outcomes:**
- **Incidence:** Number of new ALS cases per 100,000 person-years.
- **Prevalence:** Point prevalence on December 31 of each year per 100,000 beneficiaries.
- **Functional decline:** cALSFRS-R score derived from healthcare utilization trajectories (see Table 1). Score range 0–48, with higher scores indicating better function, consistent with ALSFRS-R.
- **Overall survival:** Time from index date to death (Health-10).
- **Time to invasive ventilation:** Tracheostomy or invasive mechanical ventilation >48 hours, identified from Health-02.

**Covariates:**
- Age at onset, sex, riluzole use, NIV, tracheostomy.
- Charlson Comorbidity Index (from inpatient/outpatient diagnoses in the year before index).
- Urbanization level, socioeconomic status (if available via NHIRD auxiliary files).
- Year of diagnosis.

### 3.4 Statistical Plan

#### 3.4.1 Incidence and Prevalence
- Annual incidence rates will be calculated as new cases per 100,000 person-years, stratified by age, sex, and year.
- Annual prevalence will be calculated as the number of alive ALS patients on December 31 divided by the mid-year beneficiary population.
- Poisson or negative binomial regression will be used to estimate trends over time.
- Direct age-sex standardization will be applied using the Taiwan 2016 population or WHO standard population.
- Joinpoint regression will be used to identify changes in temporal trends.

#### 3.4.2 ALSFRS-R-Equivalent Functional Decline
We will develop a claims-based ALSFRS-R-equivalent score (cALSFRS-R) by mapping the 12 ALSFRS-R domains to healthcare utilization indicators (Table 1). For each domain, we will assign a score from 0 (severe impairment) to 4 (normal function) based on the frequency and intensity of claims indicators (e.g., number of visits, procedures, medications) in each quarter. The sum will yield a 0–48 score.

Longitudinal mixed-effects models will be used to model cALSFRS-R trajectories:
- Fixed effects: time (months from index), time², age at onset, sex, riluzole, NIV, tracheostomy, baseline cALSFRS-R.
- Random effects: random intercept and random slope for time, with unstructured covariance.
- Nonlinear trajectories will be modeled using restricted cubic splines.
- Time-varying covariates (riluzole, NIV, tracheostomy) will be updated quarterly.
- Latent class mixed models will be used to identify distinct trajectory subgroups.
- A joint model of longitudinal cALSFRS-R and survival will be fitted to account for informative dropout.
- Model selection will use AIC/BIC. Missing data will be handled by mixed models under the missing-at-random assumption, with sensitivity analyses using multiple imputation.

#### 3.4.3 Survival and Time to Invasive Ventilation
- **Overall survival:** Kaplan-Meier curves with 95% confidence intervals; log-rank tests for group comparisons. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models will estimate hazard ratios for age, sex, riluzole, NIV, and tracheostomy (time-varying). The proportional hazards assumption will be checked using Schoenfeld residuals.
- **Time to invasive ventilation:** Death is a competing risk. We will use cumulative incidence function (Fine-Gray) and cause-specific Cox models. Landmark analysis at 3 and 6 months will be used to avoid immortal time bias.
- **Sensitivity analyses:** Alternative ALS definitions (e.g., requiring catastrophic illness certificate only), different washout periods, exclusion of deaths within 90 days, and treating death as censoring.

### 3.5 Sample Size and Power
Based on previous Taiwan studies, ALS incidence is approximately 1.0–2.0 per 100,000 person-years. With Taiwan’s population of ~23 million, we expect 230–460 new cases per year, or 1,150–2,300 incident cases over 5 years. Prevalence is estimated at 5–7 per 100,000, yielding ~1,150–1,610 prevalent cases. This sample size provides >80% power to detect hazard ratios of 0.7–1.4 for survival outcomes with 10 covariates. For mixed models, quarterly measurements over 5 years will yield ~20 repeated measures per patient and >20,000 observations, sufficient to model nonlinear trajectories.

### 3.6 Ethical Considerations
The study will be approved by the Institutional Review Board (IRB) of the applicant institution and the NHRI/HWDC data governance committee. All data are encrypted and de-identified. Results will be reported in aggregate to protect privacy. The study will comply with Taiwan’s Personal Data Protection Act and NHRI data usage regulations.

---

## 4. Expected Outcomes and Significance

This study will provide the first nationwide estimates of ALS incidence and prevalence in Taiwan, a novel claims-based tool for monitoring functional decline, and robust estimates of survival and time to invasive ventilation. It will clarify the real-world impact of riluzole, NIV, and tracheostomy, and identify subgroups at higher risk of rapid progression. The findings will inform clinical decision-making, resource allocation, and health policy for ALS care in Taiwan and other Asian populations.

---

## 5. Limitations

- Claims data lack direct ALSFRS-R measurements; cALSFRS-R is a proxy and may not perfectly correlate with clinical severity.
- Coding errors and undercoding of rare diseases may lead to misclassification.
- NIV and tracheostomy procedure codes may vary across hospitals.
- Cause of death may be misclassified.
- No genetic, lifestyle, or detailed socioeconomic data.
- Possible informative censoring and unmeasured confounding.
